export const DEFAULT_TREASURY_ADDRESSES = {
  solana: process.env.TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS || 'WAKETreasurySolana1111111111111111111111111',
  polygon: process.env.TREASURY_POLYGON_ADDRESS || '0xWAKETreasuryPolygon00000000000000000000000'
} as const;

/**
 * On-chain EVM / Polygon USDC verification using viem.
 */
export async function verifyPolygonUsdcTransferOnChain(input: {
  txHash: string;
  expectedUsdc: number;
  treasuryAddress: string;
}): Promise<{ verified: boolean; payerAddress: string | null; amountUsdc: number }> {
  try {
    return await executeWithRpcFailover({
      chain: 'polygon',
      action: async (rpcUrl) => {
        const { createPublicClient, http, parseAbiItem } = await import('viem');
        const { polygon } = await import('viem/chains');

        const client = createPublicClient({
          chain: polygon,
          transport: http(rpcUrl)
        });

        const receipt = await client.getTransactionReceipt({ hash: input.txHash as `0x${string}` });
        if (receipt.status !== 'success') {
          return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: 0 };
        }

        const transferEventAbi = parseAbiItem(
          'event Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value)'
        );

        const usdcContract = USDC_MINTS.polygon.toLowerCase();
        const treasuryLower = input.treasuryAddress.toLowerCase();

        // Scan logs for ERC-20 Transfer to treasury
        for (const log of receipt.logs) {
          if (log.address.toLowerCase() !== usdcContract) continue;
          try {
            // Topics: [0] = signature, [1] = from, [2] = to
            if (log.topics[2]) {
              const toAddress = `0x${log.topics[2].slice(26)}`.toLowerCase();
              if (toAddress === treasuryLower) {
                const rawAmount = BigInt(log.data);
                const amountUsdc = Number(rawAmount) / 1e6;
                const fromAddress = log.topics[1] ? `0x${log.topics[1].slice(26)}` : null;

                if (amountUsdc >= input.expectedUsdc) {
                  return { verified: true, payerAddress: fromAddress, amountUsdc };
                }
              }
            }
          } catch {
            // Ignore unparseable log
          }
        }

        return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: 0 };
      }
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[billing] Polygon USDC verification failed:', error);
    return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: 0 };
  }
}

interface SolanaParsedTokenBalance {
  accountIndex: number;
  mint: string;
  owner?: string;
  uiTokenAmount: {
    uiAmount: number | null;
  };
}

interface SolanaAccountKey {
  pubkey: string;
  signer: boolean;
}

interface SolanaRpcTransactionResult {
  meta?: {
    err: unknown | null;
    preTokenBalances?: SolanaParsedTokenBalance[];
    postTokenBalances?: SolanaParsedTokenBalance[];
  } | null;
  transaction?: {
    message?: {
      accountKeys?: SolanaAccountKey[];
    };
  };
}

/**
 * On-chain Solana SPL USDC verification using standard JSON-RPC.
 */
export async function verifySolanaUsdcTransferOnChain(input: {
  txHash: string;
  expectedUsdc: number;
  treasuryAddress: string;
  memo?: string | null;
}): Promise<{ verified: boolean; payerAddress: string | null; amountUsdc: number }> {
  try {
    return await executeWithRpcFailover({
      chain: 'solana',
      action: async (rpcUrl) => {
        const response = await fetch(rpcUrl, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            jsonrpc: '2.0',
            id: 'billing-verify',
            method: 'getTransaction',
            params: [
              input.txHash,
              { encoding: 'jsonParsed', maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 0 }
            ]
          })
        });

        if (!response.ok) {
          throw new Error(`Solana RPC HTTP ${response.status}: ${response.statusText}`);
        }

        const payload = (await response.json()) as {
          result?: SolanaRpcTransactionResult;
          error?: { message: string };
        };
        if (payload.error) {
          throw new Error(`Solana RPC error: ${payload.error.message}`);
        }
        const tx = payload.result;

        if (!tx || tx.meta?.err) {
          return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: 0 };
        }

        const targetMint = USDC_MINTS.solana;
        let foundAmountUsdc = 0;
        let payer: string | null = null;

        const preBalances = tx.meta?.preTokenBalances || [];
        const postBalances = tx.meta?.postTokenBalances || [];

        for (const post of postBalances) {
          if (post.mint === targetMint && post.owner === input.treasuryAddress) {
            const pre = preBalances.find((p: SolanaParsedTokenBalance) => p.accountIndex === post.accountIndex);
            const preAmount = pre?.uiTokenAmount.uiAmount || 0;
            const postAmount = post.uiTokenAmount.uiAmount || 0;
            const diff = postAmount - preAmount;
            if (diff > 0) {
              foundAmountUsdc += diff;
            }
          }
        }

        const accountKeys = tx.transaction?.message?.accountKeys || [];
        const signerAccount = accountKeys.find((k: SolanaAccountKey) => k.signer);
        if (signerAccount) {
          payer = signerAccount.pubkey;
        }

        if (foundAmountUsdc >= input.expectedUsdc) {
          return { verified: true, payerAddress: payer, amountUsdc: foundAmountUsdc };
        }

        return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: foundAmountUsdc };
      }
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[billing] Solana USDC verification failed:', error);
    return { verified: false, payerAddress: null, amountUsdc: 0 };
  }
}

const defaultVerifier: BillingDependencies['verifyOnChainPayment'] = async (input) => {
  if (input.chain === 'polygon') {
    return verifyPolygonUsdcTransferOnChain({
      txHash: input.txHash,
      expectedUsdc: input.expectedUsdc,
      treasuryAddress: input.treasuryAddress
    });
  }
  return verifySolanaUsdcTransferOnChain({
    txHash: input.txHash,
    expectedUsdc: input.expectedUsdc,
    treasuryAddress: input.treasuryAddress,
    memo: input.memo
  });
};

const defaultDependencies: BillingDependencies = {
  createPaymentIntent,
  recordCryptoPaymentAndGrantTier,
  getUserBillingStatus,
  listUserCryptoPayments,
  runTierDowngradeSweep,
  verifyOnChainPayment: defaultVerifier,
  findPaymentIntentByMemo: async (memo: string) => {
    try {
      const rows = await query<{ user_id: string; status: string }>(
        `SELECT user_id, status FROM user_payment_intents WHERE reference_memo = $1`,
        [memo]
      );
      return rows[0] ? { userId: rows[0].user_id, status: rows[0].status } : null;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
};

const verifyBodySchema = z
  .object({

    txHash: z.string().min(10).max(128),
    planId: z.enum(['operator_monthly', 'ultra_monthly', 'lifetime']),

  })

  }));

export async function registerBillingRoutes(
  app: FastifyInstance,
  deps: BillingDependencies = defaultDependencies
): Promise<void> {
  /**
   * GET /v1/billing/plans
   * Public / Authenticated catalog of available plans and payment addresses.
   */
  app.get('/v1/billing/plans', async (_req, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    return reply.send({
      plans: Object.values(BILLING_PLANS),
      acceptedCurrencies: ['USDC'],
      usdcMints: USDC_MINTS,
      treasuryAddresses: DEFAULT_TREASURY_ADDRESSES
    });
  });

  /**
   * GET /v1/billing/status
   * User-scoped: returns current tier, expiration, and active grace-period status.
   */
  app.get('/v1/billing/status', async (request, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const status = await deps.getUserBillingStatus(scope);
    return reply.send(status);
  });

  /**
   * GET /v1/billing/history
   * User-scoped: returns payment history receipts.
   */
  app.get('/v1/billing/history', async (request, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const payments = await deps.listUserCryptoPayments(scope);
    return reply.send({ payments });
  });

  /**
   * POST /v1/billing/crypto/intent
   * User-scoped: generates a unique reference memo for external / exchange deposit.
   */
  app.post('/v1/billing/crypto/intent', async (request, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const parsed = intentBodySchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: 'Invalid planId. Must be operator_monthly, ultra_monthly, or lifetime'
      });
    }

    try {
      const intent = await deps.createPaymentIntent(scope, parsed.data.planId);
      return reply.code(201).send({
        intent,
        treasuryAddresses: DEFAULT_TREASURY_ADDRESSES
      });
    } catch (error) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Failed to create payment intent'
      });
    }
  });

  /**
   * POST /v1/billing/crypto/verify
   * User-scoped: verifies on-chain transaction hash and unlocks the subscription immediately.
   */
  app.post('/v1/billing/crypto/verify', async (request, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const parsed = verifyBodySchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message || 'Invalid verification payload'
      });
    }

    const { chain, txHash, planId, memo } = parsed.data;
    const plan = resolveBillingPlan(planId);
    if (!plan) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: `Unknown plan: ${planId}` });
    }

    // H-06: Prevent payment hijacking by checking intent ownership
    const effectiveMemo = memo?.trim();
    if (effectiveMemo && deps.findPaymentIntentByMemo) {
      const intent = await deps.findPaymentIntentByMemo(effectiveMemo);
      if (intent && intent.userId !== scope.userId) {
        return reply.code(403).send({
          error: 'Forbidden',
          message: 'This payment reference memo belongs to a different user account.'
        });
      }
    }

    const treasury = DEFAULT_TREASURY_ADDRESSES[chain];

    // 1. Verify on-chain transfer
    const verification = await deps.verifyOnChainPayment({
      chain,
      txHash,
      expectedUsdc: plan.priceUsdc,
      treasuryAddress: treasury,
      memo
    });

    if (!verification.verified) {
      return reply.code(422).send({
        error: 'Unprocessable Entity',
        message: `Transaction ${txHash} on ${chain} could not be verified as a valid payment of ${plan.priceUsdc} USDC to treasury.`
      });
    }

    // 2. Record payment and upgrade tier atomically
    try {
      const result = await deps.recordCryptoPaymentAndGrantTier({
        scope,
        chain,
        txHash,
        amountUsdc: verification.amountUsdc,
        planId,
        payerAddress: verification.payerAddress,
        treasuryAddress: treasury,
        memo
      });

      return reply.code(200).send({
        success: true,
        paymentId: result.payment.id,
        tier: result.updatedTier,
        tierExpiresAt: result.updatedExpiresAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
        txHash: result.payment.txHash,
        amountUsdc: result.payment.amountUsdc
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof DuplicatePaymentTransactionError) {
        return reply.code(409).send({
          error: 'Conflict',
          message: error.message
        });
      }
      if (error instanceof UnderpaidPaymentError) {
        return reply.code(422).send({
          error: 'Unprocessable Entity',
          message: error.message
        });
      }
      request.log.error(error);
      return reply.code(500).send({
        error: 'Internal Server Error',
        message: 'Failed to record payment'
      });
    }
  });

  /**
   * POST /v1/admin/billing/sweep
   * Admin-scoped: triggers the automated tier downgrade sweep.
   */
  app.post('/v1/admin/billing/sweep', async (request, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    if (!requireRole(request, reply, 'admin')) return;
    const result = await deps.runTierDowngradeSweep();
    return reply.send({
      success: true,
      downgradedCount: result.downgradedCount,
      downgradedUserIds: result.downgradedUserIds
    });
  });
}

import Fastify, { type FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

/**
 * `../auth/plugin.js` — which is where the real `requireUser` lives, and using the
 * real one is the whole point of a tenancy test — statically imports `@swat/db`,
 * whose barrel throws `DATABASE_URL is required` while being evaluated. Hoisted so
 * it runs before that import, and `??=` so CI's real value is left alone. No query
 * is ever issued: every db function these routes call is injected, `pg` connects
 * lazily, and `client.ts` skips its shutdown handlers under NODE_ENV=test.
 */
vi.hoisted(() => {
  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??= 'postgres://swat:swat@127.0.0.1:5432/swat_route_tests';
});
import {
  missingDependenciesMessage,
  missingExecutionSettingsDependencies,
  registerExecutionSettingsRoutes,
  REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES,
  type ExecutionSettingsDependencies,
  type StoredChainExecutionSettings,
  type StoredExecutionSettings
} from './execution-settings.js';

/**
 * Route tests for the per-user execution-settings surface.
 *
 * No Postgres and no Redis: `registerExecutionSettingsRoutes` takes its database
 * surface as an argument, so what is under test here is the auth guard, the
 * schemas, the tenancy of the scope and the error→status mapping. The db layer's
 * own arithmetic is covered by `packages/db/src/position-cap.test.ts` and
 * `user-execution-settings.test.ts`.
 *
 * The auth guard is the *real* `requireUser`. The fake below only populates
 * `request.principal`, which is what `registerAuth` does after resolving a session
 * cookie; the scope is then derived by `requireUser` itself, from
 * `principal.user.id`. That is the point: a test that stubbed `requireUser` would
 * prove nothing about tenancy.
 */

const USER_A = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
const USER_B = '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222';

function storedSettings(
  overrides: Partial<StoredExecutionSettings> = {}
): StoredExecutionSettings {
  return {
    autoExecute: false,
    minSignalScore: 80,
    maxPositionPct: 5,
    maxDailyExposurePct: 25,
    stopLossPct: 20,
    rebuyCooldownSeconds: 3600,
    maxDailyWithdrawalUsd: 1000,
    maxConcurrentPositions: 5,
    killed: false,
    persisted: true,
    updatedAt: new Date('2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
    ...overrides
  };
}

const chainRow: StoredChainExecutionSettings = {
  chain: 'polygon',
  mode: 'paper',
  maxSlippageBps: 150,
  updatedAt: new Date('2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z')
};

interface Harness {
  readonly app: FastifyInstance;
  readonly deps: {
    [K in keyof ExecutionSettingsDependencies]: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
  } & ExecutionSettingsDependencies;
}

/**
 * `X-Test-User` stands in for a resolved session cookie, and `X-Test-Tier` for the
 * tier on that user's row. Both are read only inside the fake `onRequest` hook —
 * the handlers never see them, exactly as they never see a session token.
 */
async function harness(
  overrides: Partial<ExecutionSettingsDependencies> = {}
): Promise<Harness> {
  const deps = {
    getUserExecutionSettings: vi.fn(async () => storedSettings()),
    upsertUserExecutionSettings: vi.fn(async (_scope, patch) => storedSettings(patch)),
    setUserKillSwitch: vi.fn(async (_scope, killed: boolean) =>
      storedSettings({ killed })
    ),
    listUserChainExecutionSettings: vi.fn(async () => [chainRow]),
    upsertUserChainExecutionSettings: vi.fn(async (_scope, input) => ({
      ...chainRow,
      chain: input.chain,
      mode: input.mode ?? chainRow.mode,
      maxSlippageBps:
        'maxSlippageBps' in input ? input.maxSlippageBps ?? null : chainRow.maxSlippageBps
    })),
    listUserBalances: vi.fn(async () => [
      { chain: 'polygon' as const, usd: 100, fetchedAt: new Date() }
    ]),
    resolveKnownBalanceUsd: vi.fn((balances: readonly { usd: number | null }[]) =>
      balances.reduce<number | null>(
        (total, balance) => (total === null || balance.usd === null ? null : total + balance.usd),
        0
      )
    ),
    assessPositionCap: vi.fn((input: { requestedCap: number; maxPositionPct: number }) => ({
      requestedCap: input.requestedCap,
      effectiveCap: Math.min(input.requestedCap, 50),
      clampedByCeiling: input.requestedCap > 50,
      clampedByFloor: false,
      ceiling: 50,
      warnings: [],
      unassessed: []
    })),
    ...overrides
  } as unknown as Harness['deps'];

  const app = Fastify();
  app.decorateRequest('principal', undefined);
  app.addHook('onRequest', async (request) => {
    const header = request.headers['x-test-user'];
    const userId = Array.isArray(header) ? header[0] : header;
    if (!userId) return;
    const tierHeader = request.headers['x-test-tier'];
    const tier = (Array.isArray(tierHeader) ? tierHeader[0] : tierHeader) ?? 'free';
    request.principal = {
      kind: 'user',
      sessionId: 'session-1',
      user: {
        id: userId,
        tier,
        tierExpiresAt: null,
        role: 'user',
        status: 'active'
      }
    } as never;
  });
  await registerExecutionSettingsRoutes(app, deps);
  return { app, deps };
}

describe('GET /v1/me/execution-settings', () => {
  it('composes the two tables and the derived cap assessment', async () => {
    const { app, deps } = await harness();

    const response = await app.inject({

    expect(response.statusCode).toBe(200);

    expect(body.chains).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(body.positionCap).toMatchObject({ requestedCap: 5, effectiveCap: 5, ceiling: 50 });
    expect(deps.getUserExecutionSettings).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ userId: USER_A });
    expect(deps.listUserChainExecutionSettings).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ userId: USER_A });

describe('dependency resolution', () => {
  /**
   * Guards the packaging defect this whole module works around: `@swat/db` does not
   * re-export `./user-execution-settings.js` or `./user-balances.js` from its
   * barrel, so the wiring in `index.ts` must notice rather than serve routes whose
   * handlers call `undefined`.
   *
   * Tested through the pure predicate, not through `@swat/db` itself — importing
   * that barrel in a unit test throws `DATABASE_URL is required` before any
   * assertion could run, which is also why `resolveExecutionSettingsDependencies`
   * uses a dynamic import.
   */
  it('names every required export a namespace fails to provide', () => {
    expect(missingExecutionSettingsDependencies({})).toEqual([...REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES]);
    const partial = Object.fromEntries(
      REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES.filter((name) => name !== 'assessPositionCap').map((name) => [
        name,
        () => undefined
      ])
    );
    expect(missingExecutionSettingsDependencies(partial)).toEqual(['assessPositionCap']);
  });

  it('accepts a namespace that provides all of them', () => {
    const complete = Object.fromEntries(
      REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES.map((name) => [name, () => undefined])
    );
    expect(missingExecutionSettingsDependencies(complete)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('puts the exact fix in the message the 503 body carries', () => {
    const message = missingDependenciesMessage(['getUserExecutionSettings']);
    expect(message).toContain('packages/db/src/index.ts');
    expect(message).toContain("export * from './user-execution-settings.js';");
    expect(message).toContain('getUserExecutionSettings');
  });
});

describe('unwired deployment', () => {
  /**
   * When the db layer is missing, an authenticated caller gets a 503 that names the
   * fix — and an anonymous one still gets 401, so the 503 cannot be used to
   * enumerate which capabilities a deployment is missing.
   */
  it('answers 503 to a session and 401 to nobody', async () => {
    const app = Fastify();

      if (!userId) return;
      request.principal = {
        kind: 'user',

import type { FastifyInstance, FastifyReply } from 'fastify';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { chainSchema, type Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { requireUser } from '../auth/plugin.js';

/**
 * Per-user execution settings over HTTP (`S4-M4`, `S6-24`, `S6-25`).
 *
 * `packages/db` has held the whole layer since migration `049` —
 * `getUserExecutionSettings`, `upsertUserExecutionSettings`, `setUserKillSwitch`,
 * `listUserChainExecutionSettings`, `upsertUserChainExecutionSettings` — with no
 * caller anywhere in the repo. Every field was unreachable, which made the
 * per-user concurrent-position cap a column nobody could set.
 *
 * ## Why a separate file rather than `routes/me.ts`
 *
 * `registerMeRoutes` takes two BullMQ queues in its options. Settings need
 * neither, and folding them in would mean a settings test had to construct queue
 * plumbing to reach a validator. The split is along the dependency seam, not the
 * URL: these routes still live under `/v1/me/`, so the `USER_REACHABLE_PREFIXES`
 * allowlist in `auth/plugin.ts` already admits them and `registerAdminOnlyGlobals`
 * does not have to learn a new prefix.
 *
 * ## Why the db functions arrive as an argument
 *
 * `ExecutionSettingsDependencies` is the entire database surface these handlers
 * touch, injected. Two reasons, and the second is not hypothetical:
 *
 *   1. The route tests then exercise the real auth guard, the real zod schemas and
 *      the real status mapping with no Postgres and no Redis. A static
 *      `import … from '@swat/db'` is not free in a test: `@swat/db`'s barrel
 *      evaluates `client.ts`, which throws `DATABASE_URL is required` at import
 *      time. So the seam is what makes these routes testable at all.
 *   2. **`@swat/db` does not export this layer.** `packages/db/src/index.ts`
 *      re-exports `./position-cap.js` but *not* `./user-execution-settings.js` and
 *      *not* `./user-balances.js`; the built `packages/db/dist/index.d.ts` is older
 *      still and has no `position-cap` either. So
 *      `import { getUserExecutionSettings } from '@swat/db'` neither type-checks
 *      nor resolves today. `resolveExecutionSettingsDependencies` looks the
 *      functions up by name at boot and reports precisely which are missing; see
 *      its doc comment for what happens then.
 */

/** Mirrors `UserExecutionSettings` in `packages/db/src/user-execution-settings.ts`. */
export interface StoredExecutionSettings {
  readonly autoExecute: boolean;
  readonly minSignalScore: number;
  readonly maxPositionPct: number;
  readonly maxDailyExposurePct: number;
  readonly stopLossPct: number;
  readonly rebuyCooldownSeconds: number;
  readonly maxDailyWithdrawalUsd: number;
  readonly maxConcurrentPositions: number;
  readonly killed: boolean;
  readonly persisted: boolean;
  readonly updatedAt: Date | null;
}

/** Mirrors `UserChainExecutionSettings`. */
export interface StoredChainExecutionSettings {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly mode: 'off' | 'paper' | 'live';
  readonly maxSlippageBps: number | null;
  readonly updatedAt: Date;
}

/**
 * The subset of `UserBalance` this route reads.
 *
 * Deliberately not the whole record: the rows are grouped by chain and handed
 * straight back to `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`, which is the only thing allowed to
 * decide whether a set of rows adds up to a number the caller may use.
 */
export interface StoredBalance {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly usd: number | null;
  readonly fetchedAt: Date;
}

/** Mirrors `PositionCapAssessment` in `packages/db/src/position-cap.ts`. */
export interface PositionCapAssessmentLike {
  readonly requestedCap: number;
  readonly effectiveCap: number;
  readonly clampedByCeiling: boolean;
  readonly clampedByFloor: boolean;
  readonly ceiling: number;
  readonly warnings: readonly unknown[];
  readonly unassessed: readonly unknown[];
}

export interface ExecutionSettingsPatchInput {
  readonly autoExecute?: boolean;
  readonly minSignalScore?: number;
  readonly maxPositionPct?: number;
  readonly maxDailyExposurePct?: number;
  readonly stopLossPct?: number;
  readonly rebuyCooldownSeconds?: number;
  readonly maxDailyWithdrawalUsd?: number;
  readonly maxConcurrentPositions?: number;
}

export interface ChainExecutionSettingsInput {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly mode?: 'off' | 'paper' | 'live';
  readonly maxSlippageBps?: number | null;
  /** From the session's user row. Never from a payload. */
  readonly tier: string;
  readonly tierExpiresAt: Date | null;
}

/**
 * A `UserScope`, structurally.
 *
 * Declared here rather than imported so this module compiles against the current
 * `@swat/db` build. The scope handed to every function below still comes from
 * `requireUser`, i.e. from `forUser()`, which is the only constructor for a real
 * `UserScope`.
 */
export interface ScopeLike {
  readonly userId: string;
}

export interface ExecutionSettingsDependencies {
  readonly getUserExecutionSettings: (scope: ScopeLike) => Promise<StoredExecutionSettings>;
  readonly upsertUserExecutionSettings: (
    scope: ScopeLike,
    patch: ExecutionSettingsPatchInput
  ) => Promise<StoredExecutionSettings>;
  readonly setUserKillSwitch: (
    scope: ScopeLike,
    killed: boolean
  ) => Promise<StoredExecutionSettings>;
  readonly listUserChainExecutionSettings: (
    scope: ScopeLike
  ) => Promise<readonly StoredChainExecutionSettings[]>;
  readonly upsertUserChainExecutionSettings: (
    scope: ScopeLike,
    input: ChainExecutionSettingsInput
  ) => Promise<StoredChainExecutionSettings>;
  readonly listUserBalances: (scope: ScopeLike) => Promise<readonly StoredBalance[]>;
  readonly resolveKnownBalanceUsd: (balances: readonly StoredBalance[]) => number | null;
  readonly assessPositionCap: (input: {
    readonly requestedCap: number;
    readonly balancesUsd: Partial<Readonly<Record<Chain, number | null>>>;
    readonly maxPositionPct: number;
  }) => PositionCapAssessmentLike;
}

/**
 * Every name this module needs out of `@swat/db`.
 *
 * A list rather than eight destructured imports because the barrel does not carry
 * them yet — see the module comment. Each one is verified to exist in
 * `packages/db/src`:
 * `getUserExecutionSettings`, `upsertUserExecutionSettings`, `setUserKillSwitch`,
 * `listUserChainExecutionSettings`, `upsertUserChainExecutionSettings` in
 * `user-execution-settings.ts`; `listUserBalances`, `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` in
 * `user-balances.ts`; `assessPositionCap` in `position-cap.ts`.
 */
export const REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES = [
  'getUserExecutionSettings',
  'upsertUserExecutionSettings',
  'setUserKillSwitch',
  'listUserChainExecutionSettings',
  'upsertUserChainExecutionSettings',
  'listUserBalances',
  'resolveKnownBalanceUsd',
  'assessPositionCap'
] as const;

/**
 * Which of `REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES` a module namespace does not provide as a
 * function.
 *
 * Pure and exported so it is testable without importing `@swat/db` — which cannot
 * be imported in a unit test at all, since its barrel throws
 * `DATABASE_URL is required` on evaluation.
 */
export function missingExecutionSettingsDependencies(
  namespace: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>
): readonly string[] {
  return REQUIRED_DEPENDENCIES.filter((name) => typeof namespace[name] !== 'function');
}

export type ResolvedExecutionSettingsDependencies =
  | { readonly ok: true; readonly dependencies: ExecutionSettingsDependencies }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly missing: readonly string[] };

/**
 * What `registerExecutionSettingsRoutes` accepts in place of resolving `@swat/db`
 * itself: either the dependencies, or an already-resolved result.
 *
 * The second arm exists so the unwired-deployment behaviour (503, not 500) is
 * testable deterministically. Asserting it through the real resolver would make
 * the test pass only for as long as the barrel stays broken, and silently invert
 * the day somebody fixes it.
 */
export type ExecutionSettingsWiring =
  | ExecutionSettingsDependencies
  | ResolvedExecutionSettingsDependencies;

function normaliseWiring(
  wiring: ExecutionSettingsWiring
): ResolvedExecutionSettingsDependencies {
  // `ExecutionSettingsDependencies` has no `ok`, so the key is an unambiguous tag.
  return 'ok' in wiring ? wiring : { ok: true, dependencies: wiring };
}

/**
 * Human-readable instruction for the packaging defect, used in the boot log and
 * in the 503 body so whoever sees either knows the exact fix.
 */
export function missingDependenciesMessage(missing: readonly string[]): string {
  return (
    `@swat/db does not export ${missing.join(', ')}. `
    + "Add `export * from './user-execution-settings.js';` and "
    + "`export * from './user-balances.js';` to packages/db/src/index.ts, "
    + 'then rebuild @swat/db.'
  );
}

/**
 * Picks the real db functions out of `@swat/db` by name.
 *
 * Three deliberate choices here, all forced by the same defect:
 *
 *   * **A dynamic `import()`, not a static one.** A static import would evaluate
 *     `client.ts` in every test that so much as touches this file. `index.ts`
 *     already imports `@swat/db` statically, so at boot this is a module-cache hit
 *     and costs nothing.
 *   * **Looked up through a `Record<string, unknown>` view.** Three of the eight
 *     names are absent from the barrel, so a named import or a `db.assessPositionCap`
 *     member access would be a compile error. This is neither, and it still cannot
 *     ship a silently broken route because every name is checked.
 *   * **Returns a result, does not throw.** The alternative — refusing to boot —
 *     would take the whole control plane down over a settings feature. The repo
 *     reserves boot-time refusal for security invariants (`API_KEY` in production);
 *     a missing barrel export is not one. So the failure is confined to these four
 *     routes, which answer 503 with the fix in the body, and is logged loudly once
 *     at registration. What is NOT acceptable, and what this exists to prevent, is
 *     a route that calls `undefined` and returns 500 while looking like a bug in
 *     this file.
 *
 * Delete this and use named imports once the barrel carries the two modules.
 */
export async function resolveExecutionSettingsDependencies(): Promise<
  ResolvedExecutionSettingsDependencies
> {
  const namespace = (await import('@swat/db')) as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
  const missing = missingExecutionSettingsDependencies(namespace);
  if (missing.length > 0) return { ok: false, missing };
  return { ok: true, dependencies: namespace as unknown as ExecutionSettingsDependencies };
}

/**
 * The global patch schema.
 *
 * `.strict()` on purpose. A settings PATCH is the one place where an ignored
 * unknown key is actively dangerous: `maxPositionPCT: 1` would be silently
 * dropped and the user told their risk limit had been saved. Rejecting the body is
 * the only answer that cannot mislead — and it is also what closes the
 * `"userId": "<someone else>"` shape, which is refused rather than merely ignored.
 *
 * Bounds are deliberately NOT restated here. `assertValidExecutionSettingsPatch`
 * in `packages/db` owns them, mirrored by the column CHECKs in `049`, and a second
 * copy would drift. What this schema owns is *types*: a string where a number
 * belongs must not reach SQL.
 *
 * **`killed` is deliberately absent.** See the kill-switch route.
 */
const patchSchema = z
  .object({
    autoExecute: z.boolean().optional(),
    minSignalScore: z.number().optional(),
    maxPositionPct: z.number().optional(),
    maxDailyExposurePct: z.number().optional(),
    stopLossPct: z.number().optional(),
    rebuyCooldownSeconds: z.number().optional(),
    maxDailyWithdrawalUsd: z.number().optional(),
    maxConcurrentPositions: z.number().optional()
  })
  .strict();

const killSwitchSchema = z.object({ killed: z.boolean() }).strict();

const chainPatchSchema = z
  .object({
    mode: z.enum(['off', 'paper', 'live']).optional(),
    // `.nullable()` AND `.optional()`, because the column distinguishes them:
    // `null` clears the override back to the chain default, an absent key leaves
    // the stored value alone. Collapsing the two would make "use the default" and
    // "don't touch it" the same request.
    maxSlippageBps: z.number().int().nullable().optional()
  })
  .strict();

/**
 * Maps a db-layer validation error to a status code, by `name`.
 *
 * By `name` rather than `instanceof` because both error classes can exist twice in
 * one process while the barrel is incomplete — a class reached through a deep
 * import is not the class reached through the package root, and `instanceof` across
 * the two is false. Both classes set `this.name` explicitly, so the name is the
 * stable discriminator, and it keeps this module free of an import it cannot make.
 *
 * `InvalidExecutionSettingsError` and `InvalidPositionCapError` are **400**: a user
 * asking for 500 concurrent positions or a 150% stop loss has made a bad request,
 * not triggered a server fault. `LiveExecutionNotEntitledError` is **403** — the
 * request is well formed and the answer is still no. Anything else is rethrown so
 * Fastify turns it into a 500; reporting an unknown failure as a 400 would tell the
 * user their input was wrong and leave them retyping a valid value forever.
 */
export function settingsErrorStatus(error: unknown): 400 | 403 | null {
  if (!(error instanceof Error)) return null;
  if (error.name === 'InvalidExecutionSettingsError') return 400;
  if (error.name === 'InvalidPositionCapError') return 400;
  if (error.name === 'LiveExecutionNotEntitledError') return 403;
  return null;
}

function sendSettingsError(reply: FastifyReply, error: unknown): FastifyReply {
  const status = settingsErrorStatus(error);
  if (status === null) throw error;
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Invalid request';
  return reply
    .code(status)
    .send({ error: status === 400 ? 'Bad Request' : 'Forbidden', message });
}

/**
 * Per-chain USD totals for `assessPositionCap`.
 *
 * Grouped here, summed by `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`, which returns `null` on any
 * stale or unpriced row rather than a partial total. A chain absent from the result
 * is *unknown* to the assessment and lands in its `unassessed` list. The one thing
 * that must never happen is an unknown balance reading as a passing check.
 */
function balancesUsdByChain(
  deps: ExecutionSettingsDependencies,
  balances: readonly StoredBalance[]
): Partial<Record<Chain, number | null>> {
  const grouped = new Map<Chain, StoredBalance[]>();
  for (const balance of balances) {
    const existing = grouped.get(balance.chain);
    if (existing) existing.push(balance);
    else grouped.set(balance.chain, [balance]);
  }
  const result: Partial<Record<Chain, number | null>> = {};
  for (const [chain, rows] of grouped) {
    result[chain] = deps.resolveKnownBalanceUsd(rows);
  }
  return result;
}

/**
 * The derived cap warning (`S4-M4`, `S6-25`), returned at the point of
 * configuration rather than discovered later in a skip reason.
 *
 * `null` means **not assessed**, never "assessed and fine" — the caller renders
 * nothing rather than a reassuring absence of warnings. Degrading to `null` instead
 * of propagating is deliberate for exactly one class of failure, the balance cache:
 * the warning is advisory by construction, so a settings page that will not render
 * because `user_balances` hiccuped is strictly worse than one that renders without
 * the hint. The failure is logged.
 */
async function assessStoredCap(
  deps: ExecutionSettingsDependencies,
  scope: ScopeLike,
  settings: StoredExecutionSettings,
  requestedCap: number,
  log: { warn: (obj: unknown, message: string) => void }
): Promise<PositionCapAssessmentLike | null> {
  try {
    const balances = await deps.listUserBalances(scope);
    return deps.assessPositionCap({
      requestedCap,
      balancesUsd: balancesUsdByChain(deps, balances),
      maxPositionPct: settings.maxPositionPct
    });
  } catch (error) {
    log.warn({ err: error }, 'position cap assessment unavailable');
    return null;
  }
}

export async function registerExecutionSettingsRoutes(
  app: FastifyInstance,
  wiring?: ExecutionSettingsWiring
): Promise<void> {
  const resolved = wiring
    ? normaliseWiring(wiring)
    : await resolveExecutionSettingsDependencies();
  const deps: ExecutionSettingsDependencies | null = resolved.ok ? resolved.dependencies : null;
  const unavailable = resolved.ok ? null : missingDependenciesMessage(resolved.missing);
  if (unavailable) app.log.error({ missing: resolved.ok ? [] : resolved.missing }, unavailable);

  /**
   * Asserts the db layer is actually wired.
   *
   * Called *after* `requireUser` in every handler, so an anonymous caller gets 401
   * rather than a 503 that discloses which capabilities this deployment is missing.
   */
  function available(reply: FastifyReply): ExecutionSettingsDependencies | null {
    if (deps) return deps;
    reply.code(503).send({ error: 'Service Unavailable', message: unavailable });
    return null;
  }

  /**
   * Global settings, per-chain rows and the derived cap warning in one response.
   *
   * Two reads, never a join. `user_execution_settings` and
   * `user_chain_execution_settings` are separate tables read separately on purpose
   * — the fan-out enumeration wants the per-chain rows for many users while the
   * withdrawal path wants one user's caps — so they are composed here, at the one
   * caller that genuinely needs both, rather than joined in SQL where every other
   * caller would start paying for the other table's columns.
   */
  app.get('/v1/me/execution-settings', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const wired = available(reply);
    if (!wired) return;
    const [settings, chains] = await Promise.all([
      wired.getUserExecutionSettings(scope),
      wired.listUserChainExecutionSettings(scope)
    ]);
    const positionCap = await assessStoredCap(
      wired,
      scope,
      settings,
      settings.maxConcurrentPositions,
      request.log
    );
    return reply.send({ settings, chains, positionCap });
  });

  /**
   * Patches the global row.
   *
   * An **empty body is a 400**, not a no-op. The insert side of
   * `upsertUserExecutionSettings` creates the row, which flips `persisted` to true
   * — and `persisted` is the evidence that the user explicitly accepted these
   * limits (D13). A `PATCH {}` would manufacture that evidence without the user
   * having chosen anything.
   *
   * The response re-assesses the cap against the value the *request* asked for, so
   * `clampedByCeiling` / `clampedByFloor` are meaningful: a user who typed 500 is
   * told the stored value is 50, and why, at the slider — instead of finding out
   * from a skip reason days later.
   */
  app.patch('/v1/me/execution-settings', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const wired = available(reply);
    if (!wired) return;

    const parsed = patchSchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      const namedKilled =
        typeof request.body === 'object'
        && request.body !== null
        && 'killed' in (request.body as Record<string, unknown>);
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: namedKilled
          ? 'killed is set through PUT /v1/me/execution-settings/kill-switch'
          : 'Invalid execution settings payload',
        issues: parsed.error.issues.map((issue) => ({
          path: issue.path.join('.'),
          message: issue.message
        }))
      });
    }
    if (Object.keys(parsed.data).length === 0) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: 'No execution settings fields supplied' });
    }

    let settings: StoredExecutionSettings;
    try {
      settings = await wired.upsertUserExecutionSettings(scope, parsed.data);
    } catch (error) {
      return sendSettingsError(reply, error);
    }

    const positionCap = await assessStoredCap(
      wired,
      scope,
      settings,
      parsed.data.maxConcurrentPositions ?? settings.maxConcurrentPositions,
      request.log
    );
    return reply.send({ settings, positionCap });
  });

  /**
   * The per-user kill switch (`S6-8`), on its own path.
   *
   * It gets its own endpoint for the same reason it gets its own db helper: "stop
   * everything now" must not be able to fail on an unrelated field's validation.
   * Folded into the global PATCH, a body of
   * `{ killed: true, maxPositionPct: 150 }` returns 400 with nothing stopped —
   * precisely the outcome `setUserKillSwitch` exists to make impossible. So
   * `killed` is excluded from `patchSchema` and a body naming it is refused with a
   * pointer here; there is exactly one way to halt an account, and it validates one
   * boolean.
   *
   * `PUT`, not `POST`: the request states the desired state and is idempotent, so a
   * client retrying after a timeout cannot toggle the switch back on.
   *
   * Registered before `/chains/:chain`. The two do not actually collide, but the
   * house rule here is static-before-parameterised (see `/v1/signals/stats` in
   * `index.ts`), and a later `:something` sibling under this prefix would shadow
   * this path.
   */
  app.put('/v1/me/execution-settings/kill-switch', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const wired = available(reply);
    if (!wired) return;
    const parsed = killSwitchSchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: 'Body must be exactly { killed: boolean }' });
    }
    try {
      const settings = await wired.setUserKillSwitch(scope, parsed.data.killed);
      return reply.send({ settings });
    } catch (error) {
      return sendSettingsError(reply, error);
    }
  });

  /**
   * Patches one chain's mode and slippage override.
   *
   * The chain comes from the path and is validated against `chainSchema` rather
   * than trusted — it reaches a `VARCHAR(32)` guarded by `chk_uces_chain`, and an
   * unvalidated value would surface as a 23514 naming a constraint the caller has
   * never heard of.
   *
   * `tier` and `tierExpiresAt` come from `request.principal.user`, never from the
   * body: they are the *entitlement* the live-mode gate reads, so accepting them
   * from a payload would let any user grant themselves live execution by typing
   * `"tier": "ultra"`. `.strict()` refuses such a body outright rather than
   * quietly dropping the key. Storing `live` is still only a request —
   * `resolveChainMode` clamps it against `LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` and the chain
   * certification before anything executes.
   */
  app.patch('/v1/me/execution-settings/chains/:chain', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const principal = request.principal;
    if (principal?.kind !== 'user') return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'Unauthorized' });
    const wired = available(reply);
    if (!wired) return;

    const chainParsed = chainSchema.safeParse((request.params as { chain?: unknown }).chain);
    if (!chainParsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: 'Unknown chain' });
    }
    const bodyParsed = chainPatchSchema.safeParse(request.body ?? {});
    if (!bodyParsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: 'Invalid chain execution settings payload',
        issues: bodyParsed.error.issues.map((issue) => ({
          path: issue.path.join('.'),
          message: issue.message
        }))
      });
    }
    if (Object.keys(bodyParsed.data).length === 0) {
      return reply
        .code(400)
        .send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: 'No chain execution settings fields supplied' });
    }

    // Built key-by-key rather than spread, because `upsertUserChainExecutionSettings`
    // reads `maxSlippageBps !== undefined` to tell "clear the override" (`null`)
    // from "leave it alone" (absent). A spread of a parsed object that happened to
    // carry an explicit `undefined` would collapse the two.
    const input: {
      chain: Chain;
      tier: string;
      tierExpiresAt: Date | null;
      mode?: 'off' | 'paper' | 'live';
      maxSlippageBps?: number | null;
    } = {
      chain: chainParsed.data,
      tier: principal.user.tier,
      tierExpiresAt: principal.user.tierExpiresAt
    };
    if (bodyParsed.data.mode !== undefined) input.mode = bodyParsed.data.mode;
    if ('maxSlippageBps' in bodyParsed.data) {
      input.maxSlippageBps = bodyParsed.data.maxSlippageBps ?? null;
    }

    try {
      const chain = await wired.upsertUserChainExecutionSettings(scope, input);
      return reply.send({ chain });
    } catch (error) {
      return sendSettingsError(reply, error);
    }
  });
}

export interface StoredWithdrawalOtp {
  code: string;
  expiresAt: Date;
  destinationAddress: string;
  chainKind: string;
  amountUsd?: number;
  attempts: number;
}

export interface MeRouteOptions {
  readonly backfillQueue: Queue;
  readonly tokenDiscoveryQueue: Queue;
  readonly now?: () => Date;
  readonly coolingOffMs?: number;
  readonly otpStore?: Map<string, StoredWithdrawalOtp>;
  readonly sendWithdrawalOtpEmail?: (email: string, code: string) => Promise<boolean>;
}

export const DEFAULT_WITHDRAWAL_COOLING_OFF_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours (S4-12)

export function isSameAddress(a: string, b: string, chainKind: string): boolean {
  if (chainKind === 'solana') {
    return a.trim() === b.trim();
  }
  return a.trim().toLowerCase() === b.trim().toLowerCase();
}

export function constantTimeCodeMatch(a: string, b: string): boolean {
  if (typeof a !== 'string' || typeof b !== 'string' || a.length !== b.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(a), Buffer.from(b));
}

export function isWalletCoolingOff(
  verifiedAt: Date,
  now: Date = new Date(),
  coolingOffMs: number = DEFAULT_WITHDRAWAL_COOLING_OFF_MS
): { isCoolingOff: boolean; hoursRemaining: number } {
  const ageMs = now.getTime() - verifiedAt.getTime();
  if (ageMs < coolingOffMs) {
    const hoursRemaining = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((coolingOffMs - ageMs) / (60 * 60 * 1000)));
    return { isCoolingOff: true, hoursRemaining };
  }
  return { isCoolingOff: false, hoursRemaining: 0 };
}

export async function registerMeRoutes(
  app: FastifyInstance,

  // ─── User Profile & Dashboard State ──────────────────────────────────────────
  app.get('/v1/me/account', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const principal = request.principal;
    if (principal?.kind !== 'user') return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'Unauthorized' });

    const user = {
      id: principal.user.id,
      email: principal.user.email,
      displayName: principal.user.displayName,
      role: principal.user.role,
      tier: principal.user.tier,
      createdAt: principal.user.createdAt,
      tierExpiresAt: principal.user.tierExpiresAt
    };

    const balanceRows = await query<{
      chain: string;
      asset: string;
      amount: string;
      usd: string | null;
      fetched_at: Date;
    }>(
      `SELECT chain, asset, amount, usd, fetched_at
         FROM user_balances
        WHERE user_id = $1
        ORDER BY chain, asset`,
      [scope.userId]
    );

    const defaultChains = [
      { chain: 'solana', asset: 'USDC', balanceUsd: 0, balanceNative: 0 },
      { chain: 'robinhood-chain', asset: 'USDC', balanceUsd: 0, balanceNative: 0 },
      { chain: 'polygon', asset: 'USDC', balanceUsd: 0, balanceNative: 0 }
    ];

    const balances = balanceRows.length > 0
      ? balanceRows.map((b) => ({
          chain: b.chain,
          asset: b.asset,
          balanceUsd: b.usd != null ? Number(b.usd) : Number(b.amount || 0),
          balanceNative: Number(b.amount || 0),
          updatedAt: b.fetched_at ? new Date(b.fetched_at).toISOString() : new Date().toISOString()
        }))
      : defaultChains.map((d) => ({
          ...d,
          updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()
        }));

    const subscriptions = await query<{
      wallet_address: string;
      chain: string | null;
      label: string | null;
      state: string;
      membership_slot: number | null;
      composite_score: number | null;
      tier: string | null;
      win_rate: number | null;
      realized_roi: number | null;
      total_trades: number | null;
    }>(
      `SELECT uws.wallet_address, COALESCE(w.chain, 'solana') AS chain,
              uws.label, uws.state, uws.membership_slot,
              w.composite_score, w.tier, w.win_rate, w.realized_roi, w.total_trades
         FROM user_wallet_subscriptions uws
         LEFT JOIN wallets w ON w.address = uws.wallet_address
        WHERE uws.user_id = $1 AND uws.state = 'active'
        ORDER BY uws.created_at DESC`,
      [scope.userId]
    );

    const [settingsRow] = await query<{
      killed: boolean;
      max_slippage_bps: number;
      max_position_pct: number;
    }>(
      `SELECT ues.killed, ues.max_position_pct,
              COALESCE((SELECT uces.max_slippage_bps FROM user_chain_execution_settings uces WHERE uces.user_id = ues.user_id LIMIT 1), 100) AS max_slippage_bps
         FROM user_execution_settings ues
        WHERE ues.user_id = $1`,
      [scope.userId]
    );

    return reply.send({
      user,
      balances,
      subscriptions: subscriptions.map((s) => ({
        walletAddress: s.wallet_address,
        chain: s.chain || 'solana',
        label: s.label,
        state: s.state,
        membershipSlot: s.membership_slot,
        compositeScore: s.composite_score != null ? Number(s.composite_score) : null,
        tier: s.tier || 'speculative',
        winRate: s.win_rate != null ? Number((Number(s.win_rate) * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
        realizedRoi: s.realized_roi != null ? Number((Number(s.realized_roi) * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
        totalTrades: s.total_trades != null ? Number(s.total_trades) : 0
      })),
      executionSettings: {
        killSwitchActive: settingsRow?.killed ?? false,
        maxSlippageBps: settingsRow?.max_slippage_bps ?? 100,
        maxPositionPct: settingsRow?.max_position_pct ?? 10
      }
    });
  });

  // ─── Open Positions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  app.get('/v1/me/positions', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;

    const positions = await query<{
      id: string;
      chain: string;
      token_mint: string;
      confirmed_quantity: string;
      cost_basis_usd: string;
      token_symbol: string | null;
      master_wallet_address: string | null;

    }>(

              tm.symbol AS token_symbol,
              cpm.master_wallet_address,
              ps.price_usd AS latest_price_usd
         FROM copy_positions cp
         LEFT JOIN tokens tm ON tm.mint = cp.token_mint
         LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
           SELECT master_wallet_address
             FROM copy_position_master_lots
            WHERE position_id = cp.id AND remaining_quantity > 0
            LIMIT 1
         ) cpm ON true
         LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
           SELECT price_usd
             FROM price_snapshots
            WHERE token_mint = cp.token_mint AND chain = cp.chain
            ORDER BY snapshot_at DESC
            LIMIT 1
         ) ps ON true
        WHERE cp.user_id = $1 AND cp.confirmed_quantity > 0
        ORDER BY cp.cost_basis_usd DESC`,
      [scope.userId]
    );

    return reply.send({
      positions: positions.map((p) => {
        const confirmedQuantity = Number(p.confirmed_quantity || 0);
        const costBasisUsd = Number(p.cost_basis_usd || 0);
        const entryPriceUsd = confirmedQuantity > 0 ? costBasisUsd / confirmedQuantity : 0;
        const currentPriceUsd = p.latest_price_usd != null ? Number(p.latest_price_usd) : null;
        const currentValueUsd = currentPriceUsd != null ? confirmedQuantity * currentPriceUsd : costBasisUsd;
        const unrealizedPnlUsd = currentPriceUsd != null ? currentValueUsd - costBasisUsd : null;
        const unrealizedPnlPct = (currentPriceUsd != null && costBasisUsd > 0)
          ? ((unrealizedPnlUsd! / costBasisUsd) * 100)
          : null;

        return {
          id: p.id,
          chain: p.chain,
          tokenMint: p.token_mint,
          tokenSymbol: p.token_symbol || p.token_mint.slice(0, 8),
          confirmedQuantity,
          costBasisUsd,
          entryPriceUsd,
          currentPriceUsd,
          unrealizedPnlUsd,
          unrealizedPnlPct,
          masterWalletAddress: p.master_wallet_address || undefined
        };
      })
    });
  });

  app.post('/v1/me/vault/revoke', async (request, reply) => {

  // ─── Polymarket CLOB L2 Authentication ──────────────────────────────────────
  app.get('/v1/me/vault/polymarket/challenge', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;

    const q = request.query as { address?: string };
    const address = q.address?.trim();
    if (!address || !/^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$/.test(address)) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Bad Request',
        message: 'Valid EVM address query param required (0x followed by 40 hex characters)'
      });
    }

    const timestampSeconds = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
    const nonce = 0;
    const typedData = buildClobAuthTypedData({
      signerAddress: address,
      timestampSeconds,
      nonce
    });

    return reply.send({
      address,
      timestampSeconds,
      nonce,
      typedData
    });

  const polymarketCredentialsSchema = z.object({
    address: z.string().trim().regex(/^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$/),
    signature: z.string().trim().regex(/^0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$/),
    timestampSeconds: z.number().int().positive(),
    nonce: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0)
  });

  app.post('/v1/me/vault/polymarket/credentials', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;

    const parsed = polymarketCredentialsSchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Bad Request', issues: parsed.error.issues });
    }

    const { address, signature, timestampSeconds, nonce } = parsed.data;

    request.log.info(
      { address, signature, timestampSeconds, nonce },
      '[polymarket-clob] Received credentials derivation request'
    );

    try {
      const { recoverTypedDataAddress } = await import('viem');
      const recovered137 = await recoverTypedDataAddress({
        domain: { name: 'ClobAuthDomain', version: '1', chainId: BigInt(137) },
        types: {
          EIP712Domain: [
            { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'version', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' }
          ],
          ClobAuth: [
            { name: 'address', type: 'address' },
            { name: 'timestamp', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint256' },
            { name: 'message', type: 'string' }
          ]
        },
        primaryType: 'ClobAuth',
        message: {
          address: address as `0x${string}`,
          timestamp: String(timestampSeconds),
          nonce: BigInt(nonce),
          message: 'This message attests that I control the given wallet'
        },
        signature: signature as `0x${string}`
      }).catch((e: any) => `recovery_failed: ${e?.message}`);

      const recovered1 = await recoverTypedDataAddress({
        domain: { name: 'ClobAuthDomain', version: '1', chainId: BigInt(1) },
        types: {
          EIP712Domain: [
            { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'version', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' }
          ],
          ClobAuth: [
            { name: 'address', type: 'address' },
            { name: 'timestamp', type: 'string' },
            { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint256' },
            { name: 'message', type: 'string' }
          ]
        },
        primaryType: 'ClobAuth',
        message: {
          address: address as `0x${string}`,
          timestamp: String(timestampSeconds),
          nonce: BigInt(nonce),
          message: 'This message attests that I control the given wallet'
        },
        signature: signature as `0x${string}`
      }).catch((e: any) => `recovery_failed: ${e?.message}`);

      request.log.info(
        { address, recovered137, recovered1, match137: recovered137?.toLowerCase() === address.toLowerCase(), match1: recovered1?.toLowerCase() === address.toLowerCase() },
        '[polymarket-clob] Signature recovery diagnostic'
      );
    } catch (recErr) {
      request.log.warn({ err: recErr }, '[polymarket-clob] Diagnostic recovery threw');
    }

    try {
      // 1. Call Polymarket CLOB to create or derive L2 credentials using the user's signature
      const creds = await fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature({
        address,
        signature,
        timestampSeconds,
        nonce
      });

      // 2. Envelope-seal the credentials
      const wrapper = new EnvMasterKeyWrapper();
      const wrapContext: WrapContext = {
        userId: scope.userId,
        chainKind: 'evm',
        keyVersion: 1
      };
      const secretPayload = JSON.stringify({
        apiKey: creds.apiKey,
        secret: creds.secret,
        passphrase: creds.passphrase,
        signerAddress: address.toLowerCase()
      });
      const sealedSecret = await sealSecret(secretPayload, wrapContext, wrapper);

      // 3. Revoke any prior active grant for polygon polymarket_signer
      await query(
        `UPDATE user_execution_grants
            SET status = 'revoked', revoked_at = NOW()
          WHERE user_id = $1 AND chain = 'polygon' AND grant_kind = 'polymarket_signer' AND status = 'active'`,
        [scope.userId]
      );

      const policy = {
        apiKey: creds.apiKey,
        derivedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
        nonce
      };

      const inserted = await query<{ id: string }>(
        `INSERT INTO user_execution_grants
           (user_id, chain, grant_kind, account_address, sealed_secret, key_version, scope_policy, status, created_at)
         VALUES ($1, 'polygon', 'polymarket_signer', $2, $3, 1, $4, 'active', NOW())
         ON CONFLICT (chain, account_address) DO UPDATE
            SET user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id,
                sealed_secret = EXCLUDED.sealed_secret,
                key_version = EXCLUDED.key_version,
                scope_policy = EXCLUDED.scope_policy,
                status = 'active',
                revoked_at = NULL
         RETURNING id`,
        [scope.userId, address.toLowerCase(), sealedSecret, JSON.stringify(policy)]
      );

      return reply.send({
        success: true,
        grantId: inserted[0]?.id,
        address,
        apiKey: creds.apiKey,
        message: 'Polymarket L2 credentials derived and activated successfully'
      });
    } catch (err: any) {
      request.log.error(err, '[polymarket-clob] Failed to derive credentials');
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Polymarket L2 authentication failed',
        message: err.message || 'Failed to authenticate with Polymarket CLOB'
      });
    }
  });

  // ─── Suggested Alpha Masters Discovery ───────────────────────────────────────
  app.get('/v1/me/masters', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;

    const rows = await query<{
      address: string;
      chain: string;
      label: string | null;
      composite_score: number | null;
      tier: string | null;
      win_rate: number | null;
      realized_roi: number | null;
      follower_count: string;
    }>(
      `SELECT w.address, COALESCE(w.chain, 'solana') AS chain,
              COALESCE((SELECT uws.label FROM user_wallet_subscriptions uws WHERE uws.wallet_address = w.address AND uws.user_id = $1 LIMIT 1), w.nickname) AS label,
              w.composite_score, w.tier, w.win_rate, w.realized_roi,
              COUNT(DISTINCT uws.user_id) FILTER (WHERE uws.state = 'active') AS follower_count
         FROM wallets w
         LEFT JOIN user_wallet_subscriptions uws ON uws.wallet_address = w.address
        WHERE w.status = 'active'
        GROUP BY w.address, w.chain, w.nickname, w.composite_score, w.tier, w.win_rate, w.realized_roi
        ORDER BY w.composite_score DESC NULLS LAST, follower_count DESC
        LIMIT 20`,
      [scope.userId]
    );

    return reply.send({
      masters: rows.map((r) => ({
        masterWalletAddress: r.address,
        chain: r.chain,
        label: r.label,
        compositeScore: r.composite_score,
        tier: r.tier || 'pro',
        winRate: r.win_rate != null ? Number((r.win_rate * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
        realizedRoi: r.realized_roi != null ? Number((r.realized_roi * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
        followerCount: Number(r.follower_count || 0),

      }))
    });

  app.get('/v1/me/wallets', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const subscriptions = await listWalletSubscriptions(scope);
    if (subscriptions.length === 0) return reply.send({ wallets: [] });

    // Subscriptions are per-user; the wallet's stats are global. Joined here
    // rather than duplicated per user — that is the whole point of the
    // global-dedup model (D9).
    const rows = await query<{
      address: string;
      chain: Chain;
      status: string;
      composite_score: number | null;
      tier: string | null;

      last_active: Date | null;
    }>(
      `SELECT address, chain, status, composite_score, tier, win_rate, realized_roi, total_trades, last_active
         FROM wallets WHERE address = ANY($1)`,
      [subscriptions.map((s) => s.walletAddress)]
    );
    const byAddress = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.address, row]));

    return reply.send({
      wallets: subscriptions.map((subscription) => {
        const wallet = byAddress.get(subscription.walletAddress);
        return {
          address: subscription.walletAddress,
          label: subscription.label,
          source: subscription.source,
          subscribedAt: subscription.createdAt,
          chain: wallet?.chain ?? null,
          status: wallet?.status ?? null,
          compositeScore: wallet?.composite_score != null ? Number(wallet.composite_score) : null,
          tier: wallet?.tier ?? null,
          winRate: wallet?.win_rate != null ? Number((Number(wallet.win_rate) * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
          realizedRoi: wallet?.realized_roi != null ? Number((Number(wallet.realized_roi) * 100).toFixed(1)) : null,
          totalTrades: wallet?.total_trades != null ? Number(wallet.total_trades) : null,
          lastActive: wallet?.last_active ?? null
        };
      })
    });

  app.post('/v1/me/wallets', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const principal = request.principal;
    if (principal?.kind !== 'user') return reply.code(401).send({ error: 'Unauthorized' });

    const parsed = subscribeSchema.safeParse(request.body);
    if (!parsed.success) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Bad Request', message: 'Invalid wallet payload' });
    }
    if (!isValidAddressForChain(parsed.data.address, parsed.data.chain)) {
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Invalid wallet' });
    }

    const capabilities = capabilitiesFor(principal.user.tier, principal.user.tierExpiresAt);
    if (!tierAllowsChain(capabilities, parsed.data.chain)) {
      // 402, not 403: this is an upgrade path, not a permanent denial.
      return reply
        .code(402)
        .send({ error: 'Upgrade required', reason: 'chain-not-in-tier', chain: parsed.data.chain });
    }

    // Store chain-prefixed, always. `resolveChainAddress` lowercases EVM and
    // preserves Solana case — never hand-build the prefix.
    const resolved = resolveChainAddress(parsed.data.address, parsed.data.chain);

    // S4-M11: Refuse exchange hubs with an actionable reason
    const hub = await checkWalletHubStatus(resolved.prefixed, resolved.raw, parsed.data.chain);
    if (hub.isHub) {
      return reply.code(400).send({
        error: 'Cannot subscribe to exchange hub',
        reason: 'exchange-hub-refused',
        message: hub.reason
      });
    }

    // S4-M10: Advisory cluster independence warning
    const independence = await checkWalletClusterIndependence(resolved.prefixed);

    try {
      const result = await subscribeToWallet(scope, {
        walletAddress: resolved.prefixed,
        chain: parsed.data.chain,
        tier: principal.user.tier,
        tierExpiresAt: principal.user.tierExpiresAt,
        label: parsed.data.label ?? null
      });

      // Enqueue ONLY when this call created the global wallet. Enqueuing on every
      // subscribe would re-backfill a wallet each time another user tracks it,
      // which is exactly the cost the dedup model exists to avoid.
      if (result.walletCreated) {
        const job = createWalletBackfillJob(resolved.raw, parsed.data.chain);
        await options.backfillQueue.add(job.name, job.data, {
          ...job.options,
          // Lower number runs sooner; paying tiers jump the queue (D9).
          priority: capabilities.backfillPriority
        });
      }

      return reply.code(result.subscriptionCreated ? 201 : 200).send({
        wallet: {
          address: result.subscription.walletAddress,
          label: result.subscription.label,
          source: result.subscription.source,
          subscribedAt: result.subscription.createdAt
        },
        warning: independence.warning,
        backfillQueued: result.walletCreated
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) {
        return reply.code(402).send({
          error: 'Quota exceeded',
          quota: error.quota,
          limit: error.limit,
          used: error.used
        });
      }
      throw error;
    }
  });

  app.delete('/v1/me/wallets/:address', async (request, reply) => {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return;
    const { address } = request.params as { address: string };
    const q = request.query as { chain?: string };

    let candidate = address;
    if (!candidate.includes(':') && q.chain) {
      candidate = `${q.chain}:${address}`;
    }

    // Unsubscribe is an exits-only wind-down. Retaining the row preserves the
    // attribution and sell-mirror path for positions opened while active.
    try {
      let result;
      try {
        result = await beginWindDown(scope, candidate);
      } catch (err) {
        if (candidate !== address) {
          result = await beginWindDown(scope, address);
        } else {
          throw err;
        }
      }
      return reply.send({ ok: true, state: result.subscription.state });
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'WalletNotSubscribedError') {
        return reply.code(404).send({ error: 'Not subscribed' });
      }
      throw error;
    }
  });

  app.post('/v1/me/wallets/:address/close-all', async (request, reply) => {

    const q = request.query as { chain?: string };

      candidate = `${q.chain}:${address}`;
    }

    try {
      let result;

      } catch (err) {

          throw err;
        }
      }
      return reply.send({
        ok: true,
        state: result.subscription.state,
        closeAllRequestedAt: result.subscription.closeAllRequestedAt
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'WalletNotSubscribedError') {
        return reply.code(404).send({ error: 'Not subscribed' });
      }
      throw error;
    }
  });

  /**
   * Gated on subscription. Not-subscribed returns **404, not 403**: whether some
   * other user tracks a given wallet is not this user's business, and a 403 would
   * confirm the wallet exists in the platform.
   */
  async function requireSubscription(
    request: FastifyRequest,
    reply: FastifyReply
  ): Promise<{ scope: UserScope; address: string } | null> {
    const scope = requireUser(request, reply);
    if (!scope) return null;
    const { address } = request.params as { address: string };
    if (!(await isSubscribed(scope, address))) {
      reply.code(404).send({ error: 'Not found' });
      return null;
    }
    return { scope, address };
  }

  app.get('/v1/me/wallets/:address/history', async (request, reply) => {

      `SELECT signature, chain, direction, target_token, token_in, token_out,
              amount_in_usd, amount_out_usd, timestamp
         FROM transactions
        WHERE wallet_address = $1
        ORDER BY timestamp DESC
        LIMIT 200`,
      [gate.address]
    );
    return reply.send({ transactions: rows });
  });
