describe('S4-M45 — manual exit as the third entrant in the same race', () => {
  const base = {
    position: position(),
    heldShares: 40,
    masterHoldsPosition: true,
    marketResolved: false,
    acceptingOrders: true,
    manualExitRequested: false,
    existingClaim: null
  } as const;

  it('a manual request exits by the manual trigger while the book is open', () => {
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, manualExitRequested: true });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'exit',
      trigger: 'manual',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-by-manual-request'
    });
  });

  it('a manual exit racing a master sell in one observation produces exactly one exit', () => {
    // The ordinary case the item names: the user taps exit moments before the
    // master sells, and one sweep sees both. One call, one decision, one trigger —
    // there is no shape of the return type that carries two exits, which is the
    // structural half of "one race, not three paths".
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      masterHoldsPosition: false
    });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('exit');
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ trigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('manual outranks the mirrored sell, so the user\'s own instruction is what is recorded', () => {
    // Both are the same FAK sell of the whole position, so the winner does not
    // change what is sent to the venue — it changes `exit_trigger`, which
    // attribution reads. Recording the user's tap as the master's sell would show
    // the user an audit trail in which their tap did nothing.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      masterHoldsPosition: false
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ trigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('resolution still outranks a manual request, and redeems rather than selling', () => {
    // The rung that makes "Polymarket redemption is just another sell" false. The
    // user's instruction is honoured — the position exits — but a sell into a
    // resolved book cannot fill at any price, so the mechanism is redemption.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      marketResolved: true
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'exit',
      trigger: 'redemption',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-by-redemption'
    });
    expect((decision as { reason: string }).reason).toMatch(/manual request is honoured by redeeming/);
  });

  it('a manual exit does not need the master cross-reference to be readable', () => {
    // Without this the user's exit would be blocked by our own ignorance of a
    // wallet that has nothing to do with their instruction. The master-sell
    // entrant still holds on `null` — that assertion is above and unchanged.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      masterHoldsPosition: null
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'exit', trigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('a manual exit still holds when we hold no provable shares', () => {
    // Above every trigger, manual included: a user asking to exit a position we
    // cannot prove we hold must not send an order, because sizing has no honest
    // input.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      heldShares: 0
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'hold',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-proven-shares'
    });
  });

  it('the single-shot guard covers a live manual claim, so the master sell stands down', () => {
    // The other direction of the guard, and the one that proves manual entered the
    // existing race rather than sitting beside it: a claim taken by `manual` blocks
    // the mirrored-sell entrant exactly as a redemption claim does.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      masterHoldsPosition: false,
      existingClaim: { trigger: 'manual', status: 'claimed' }
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'already-exiting',
      trigger: 'manual',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-already-claimed'
    });
  });

  it('the single-shot guard covers a live manual claim against redemption too', () => {
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      marketResolved: true,
      existingClaim: { trigger: 'manual', status: 'confirmed' }
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'already-exiting', trigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('a live claim by another entrant makes the manual request stand down', () => {
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      existingClaim: { trigger: 'redemption', status: 'claimed' }
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'already-exiting', trigger: 'redemption' });
  });

  it('a failed manual claim is retryable, on the same rule as a failed redemption', () => {
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: true,
      existingClaim: { trigger: 'manual', status: 'failed' }
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'exit', trigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('a failed manual claim does not by itself become a trigger', () => {
    // The half that would go unnoticed: releasing a failed manual claim must not
    // exit a position whose market is open, whose master still holds it, and whose
    // user is no longer asking. Retryable is not the same as due.
    const decision = decidePolymarketExit({
      ...base,
      manualExitRequested: false,
      existingClaim: { trigger: 'manual', status: 'failed' }
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'hold',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-trigger-fired'
    });
  });

  it('every decision carries a stable code, not only a prose reason', () => {
    const codes = [
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, heldShares: 0 }),
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, existingClaim: { trigger: 'manual', status: 'claimed' } }),
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, marketResolved: true }),
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, manualExitRequested: true }),
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, masterHoldsPosition: false }),
      decidePolymarketExit({ ...base, masterHoldsPosition: null }),
      decidePolymarketExit(base)
    ].map((decision) => decision.code);
    expect(codes).toEqual([
      'polymarket-exit-hold-no-proven-shares',
      'polymarket-exit-already-claimed',
      'polymarket-exit-by-redemption',
      'polymarket-exit-by-manual-request',
      'polymarket-exit-by-mirrored-sell',
      'polymarket-exit-hold-master-holdings-unread',
      'polymarket-exit-hold-no-trigger-fired'
    ]);
    // Every reachable branch is covered above, so a new rung without a code fails
    // to compile and a new rung with a duplicate code fails here.
    expect(new Set(codes).size).toBe(codes.length);
  });
});

describe('S4-M45 — one claim ledger, three entrants', () => {
  /**
   * A fake standing in for the partial unique index on
   * `polymarket_position_exits (user_id, position_key) WHERE status IN
   * ('claimed','confirmed')`: the first insert for a key returns a row, every
   * later one returns null. That is the whole arbiter, and the point of these
   * tests is that all three entrants go through it.
   */
  function ledger() {
    const live = new Set<string>();
    const triggers: string[] = [];
    return {
      triggers,
      claimPositionExit: async (input: { positionKey: string; exitTrigger: string }) => {
        if (live.has(input.positionKey)) return null;
        live.add(input.positionKey);
        triggers.push(input.exitTrigger);
        return { id: `claim-${triggers.length}` };
      }
    };
  }

  it('a manual exit and a mirrored sell against one position yield exactly one winner', async () => {
    const store = ledger();
    const manual = await claimPolymarketManualExit(
      { position: position(), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    const mirrored = await claimPolymarketMirroredSellExit(
      { position: position(), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    const won = [manual, mirrored].filter((result) => result.kind === 'won');
    expect(won).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(manual).toMatchObject({ kind: 'won' });
    expect(mirrored).toMatchObject({ kind: 'lost', code: 'polymarket-exit-already-claimed' });
    // And only one row was written, under the manual trigger.
    expect(store.triggers).toEqual(['manual']);
  });

  it('the mirrored sell arriving first makes the manual exit stand down', async () => {
    // The same assertion the other way round: the winner is whoever got there
    // first, not whichever trigger this module happens to prefer.
    const store = ledger();
    const mirrored = await claimPolymarketMirroredSellExit(
      { position: position(), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    const manual = await claimPolymarketManualExit(
      { position: position(), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    expect(mirrored).toMatchObject({ kind: 'won' });
    expect(manual).toMatchObject({ kind: 'lost' });
    expect(store.triggers).toEqual(['mirrored-sell']);
  });

  it('all three entrants against one position write exactly one row', async () => {
    const store = ledger();
    const results = [];
    for (const trigger of ['manual', 'mirrored-sell', 'redemption'] as const) {
      results.push(await claimPolymarketExit(
        { position: position(), userId: null, trigger },
        { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
      ));
    }
    expect(results.filter((result) => result.kind === 'won')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(store.triggers).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('the manual entrant reaches the ledger through the same port and shape', async () => {
    // The single-path proof at the call level: identical argument object, one
    // field different. If a manual exit ever grows its own claim, this diverges.
    const calls: unknown[] = [];
    const claimPositionExit = vi.fn(async (input: unknown) => {
      calls.push(input);
      return { id: `claim-${calls.length}` };
    });
    await claimPolymarketMirroredSellExit({ position: position(), userId: 'user-1' }, { claimPositionExit });
    await claimPolymarketManualExit({ position: position(), userId: 'user-1' }, { claimPositionExit });
    expect(calls[0]).toEqual({
      positionKey: 'polygon:1001',
      conditionId: CONDITION,
      outcomeTokenId: '1001',
      exitTrigger: 'mirrored-sell',
      userId: 'user-1'
    });
    expect(calls[1]).toEqual({ ...(calls[0] as object), exitTrigger: 'manual' });
  });

  it('two outcomes of one condition each get their own manual exit', async () => {
    // A manual exit of YES must not suppress the exit of NO. The claim is keyed on
    // the outcome token, so this holds for the manual entrant exactly as `S4-M19`
    // established it for the other two.
    const store = ledger();
    const yes = await claimPolymarketManualExit(
      { position: position({ tokenId: '1001', outcome: 'Yes' }), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    const no = await claimPolymarketManualExit(
      { position: position({ tokenId: '1002', outcome: 'No' }), userId: null },
      { claimPositionExit: store.claimPositionExit }
    );
    expect(yes).toMatchObject({ kind: 'won' });
    expect(no).toMatchObject({ kind: 'won' });
    expect(store.triggers).toEqual(['manual', 'manual']);
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-exit-race.ts <==
import { UnrecoverableError } from 'bullmq';
import {
  assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct,
  parsePolymarketOutcomePosition,
  polymarketPositionKey,
  type PolymarketOutcomePosition
} from './polymarket-representation.js';

/**
 * Redemption as a first-class exit, raced against the mirrored sell
 * (checklist `S4-M19`).
 *
 * **The gap this closes.** Our copy exits today only when the master's sell is
 * mirrored. If the master holds to resolution they never sell, so there is no
 * sell to mirror and the copy never exits — the position simply sits until
 * someone notices, on an outcome that is by then worth exactly 1 or 0.
 *
 * **The decided design: two triggers, whichever fires first wins.**
 *
 *   1. the master closes their position, which mirrors as a sell today;
 *   2. the market resolves, which redeems.
 *
 * Neither alone is sufficient. Waiting only for the master's sell strands every
 * hold-to-resolution position. Waiting only for resolution exits late on every
 * position the master actually traded out of. So both are tracked and the earlier
 * one acts.
 *
 * **Single-shot per position, not per trigger.** The two triggers can fire close
 * together — a master selling moments before resolution is the ordinary case, not
 * the edge — so the race needs exactly one winner *per position*. That is what
 * `polymarket_position_exits` and `claimPolymarketPositionExit` provide: a
 * position-scoped claim with the same partial-unique-index shape as
 * `polymarket_redemptions`, which is condition-scoped and therefore cannot be the
 * guard (see below).
 *
 * **Why the claim cannot be condition-scoped.** `redeemPositions({conditionId})`
 * takes no amount and redeems the wallet's balances for *both* outcomes, so the
 * on-chain call is condition-scoped and `polymarket_redemptions` correctly guards
 * it once per condition. But a condition holds **two** outcome positions, and
 * mapping a condition-scoped result back to positions is the exact step at which
 * two outcome rows get collapsed into one. `S4-M20` says so explicitly and names
 * this as the call site for `assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct`, which
 * `mapPolymarketRedemptionToPositions` below calls, as does
 * `aggregatePolymarketExposure`.
 *
 * **The master's holdings are a cross-reference, never a source** (`S4-M37`).
 * What we are allowed to exit comes from *our* confirmed positions. Whether an
 * exit is *due* may consult whether the master still holds. Reversing that is how
 * a redemption sweep ends up trying to redeem a market we never entered.
 *
 * **Manual exit is the third entrant, not a third path** (`S4-M45`). A user
 * tapping "exit" moments before the master sells is the ordinary case, not the
 * edge, so manual exit joins *this* function and *this* claim rather than getting
 * its own. Everything below that was written for two entrants — the single-shot
 * guard, the failed-claim rule, one winner per position — covers three unchanged;
 * the only additions are one member on `PolymarketExitTrigger`, one field on the
 * race input, and one rung in the ordering. The chain-generic layer that decides
 * whether a manual exit is even expressible on a given chain lives in
 * `manual-exit.ts` and *delegates here* for Polymarket.
 *
 * Pure: no clock, no client, no database. The driver that owns the claim lives in
 * `polymarket-redemption.ts`.
 */

/** Which of the three racing triggers is acting. */
export type PolymarketExitTrigger =
  /** The master closed their position and we mirror the sell. */
  | 'mirrored-sell'
  /** The market resolved and the position redeems. */
  | 'redemption'
  /**
   * The user asked to exit, and the position sells into the book.
   *
   * Mechanically identical to `mirrored-sell` — both are a FAK sell of the whole
   * position — and deliberately kept a separate *trigger* anyway, because the two
   * record different facts. "The position exited" and "the position exited
   * because the user asked" are not the same thing, and attribution reads the
   * second one. Also: a manual exit must be able to win in states where the
   * mirrored sell is not even eligible, so it cannot be folded into it.
   */
  | 'manual';

export type PolymarketExitClaimStatus = 'claimed' | 'confirmed' | 'failed';

export interface PolymarketExitClaimState {
  readonly trigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
  readonly status: PolymarketExitClaimStatus;
}

export interface PolymarketExitRaceInput {
  readonly position: PolymarketOutcomePosition;
  /** Shares we can prove we hold. Zero means there is nothing to exit. */
  readonly heldShares: number;
  /**
   * Whether the master still holds this outcome. `null` when we have not read it
   * — which is ignorance, not evidence of a close.
   */
  readonly masterHoldsPosition: boolean | null;
  readonly marketResolved: boolean;
  readonly acceptingOrders: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether the user has asked to exit this position (`S4-M45`).
   *
   * **Required, not optional.** An omitted field defaulting to `false` can only
   * ever under-exit, so it is safe on the double-exit axis — but it is silent on
   * the other one: a caller that forgot to thread the user's request would leave
   * the user tapping "exit" and nothing happening, with no error anywhere. Every
   * caller states it.
   */
  readonly manualExitRequested: boolean;
  /** An exit already claimed for this position, if any. */
  readonly existingClaim: PolymarketExitClaimState | null;
}

/**
 * Stable outcome codes, one per reachable branch.
 *
 * Freeform `reason` strings are for a human reading a log line; these are what an
 * operator dashboard, an alert rule and `S4-M24`'s skip rendering key on. Split
 * the way `solana-simulation.ts` splits `refuse` from `unavailable`: two holds
 * that look alike in prose ("nothing happened") are different findings, and
 * sending an operator to debug the wrong one is the cost of collapsing them.
 */
export type PolymarketExitCode =
  /** We hold nothing provable, so no trigger can act. Not a fault. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-proven-shares'
  /** Another entrant already owns this position's exit. The race resolving. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-already-claimed'
  /** The market stopped accepting orders; redemption is the only exit that exists. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-by-redemption'
  /** The user asked to exit and the book is open, so it sells into the book. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-by-manual-request'
  /** The master closed and the book is open, so the exit mirrors as a sell. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-by-mirrored-sell'
  /** The master cross-reference is unread. Ignorance is not a trigger. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-hold-master-holdings-unread'
  /** Market open, master still in, no manual request. Nothing is due. */
  | 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-trigger-fired';

export type PolymarketExitRaceDecision =
  /** This trigger wins the race and should claim the position. */
  | {
    readonly kind: 'exit';
    readonly trigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
    readonly code: PolymarketExitCode;
    readonly reason: string;
  }
  /** Another trigger already won. The loser is a no-op, not an error. */
  | {
    readonly kind: 'already-exiting';
    readonly trigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
    readonly code: PolymarketExitCode;
    readonly reason: string;
  }
  /** No trigger has fired yet. */
  | { readonly kind: 'hold'; readonly code: PolymarketExitCode; readonly reason: string };

/**
 * Decide which exit trigger, if any, acts on this position now.
 *
 * **One function for all three entrants, and the ordering below is the whole
 * design.** The rungs are checked in a fixed order and the first that fires
 * returns, so exactly one trigger can win per call — and because the single-shot
 * guard sits above every one of them, exactly one can win per position across
 * calls. Adding a fourth entrant means adding a rung here, never a second
 * function.
 *
 * The order, and why each step is where it is:
 *
 *   0. **Nothing held → hold.** Above everything, including a manual request: a
 *      user asking to exit a position we cannot prove we hold must not send an
 *      order. Sizing has no honest input.
 *   1. **A live claim → stand down.** The single-shot guard. Covers all three
 *      entrants because it reads the *claim*, never the trigger being offered.
 *   2. **Resolution → redemption**, outranking both selling entrants — a venue
 *      fact, not a preference. A resolved market stops accepting orders, so a sell
 *      into it cannot fill at any price. This is the rung that makes "redemption
 *      is just another sell" false: a manual exit on a resolved market is still
 *      honoured, but it is honoured *by redeeming*, because selling is no longer
 *      a thing the venue will do.
 *   3. **Manual request → manual**, outranking the mirrored sell. Both are the
 *      same FAK sell of the whole position, so the winner does not change what is
 *      sent to the venue — it changes what is *recorded*. The user's own
 *      instruction is the more specific fact, and attributing it to the master
 *      would show the user an audit trail in which their tap did nothing. It also
 *      has to sit above rung 5: a manual exit must work when the master
 *      cross-reference is unread, and for a subscription that mirrors nothing at
 *      all.
 *   4. **Master closed → mirrored sell.**
 *   5. **Master unread → hold.** Ignorance is not a trigger.
 *   6. **Nothing due → hold.**
 */
export function decidePolymarketExit(
  input: PolymarketExitRaceInput
): PolymarketExitRaceDecision {
  const key = polymarketPositionKey(input.position);

  if (!Number.isFinite(input.heldShares) || input.heldShares <= 0) {
    return {
      kind: 'hold',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-proven-shares',
      reason: `position ${key} holds no proven shares, so there is nothing to exit`
    };
  }

  // The single-shot guard. A 'failed' claim is deliberately not a winner: a
  // redemption that failed must be retryable, and redemption has no deadline.
  //
  // It reads the claim and not the trigger being offered, which is exactly why
  // adding the manual entrant needed no change here: a manual exit arriving after
  // either other trigger claimed the position stands down, and a mirrored sell or
  // a redemption arriving after a manual claim does the same.
  if (input.existingClaim && input.existingClaim.status !== 'failed') {
    return {
      kind: 'already-exiting',
      trigger: input.existingClaim.trigger,
      code: 'polymarket-exit-already-claimed',
      reason:
        `position ${key} is already exiting via ${input.existingClaim.trigger} `
        + `(${input.existingClaim.status}); the race has one winner per position`
    };
  }

  if (input.marketResolved || !input.acceptingOrders) {
    return {
      kind: 'exit',
      trigger: 'redemption',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-by-redemption',
      reason:
        `condition ${input.position.conditionId} no longer accepts orders `
        + `(resolved=${input.marketResolved}, acceptingOrders=${input.acceptingOrders}), `
        + `so the ${input.heldShares} shares of ${input.position.outcome} exit by redemption`
        + (input.manualExitRequested
          ? ' — the manual request is honoured by redeeming, because a sell into a '
            + 'resolved book cannot fill at any price'
          : '')
    };
  }

  if (input.manualExitRequested) {
    return {
      kind: 'exit',
      trigger: 'manual',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-by-manual-request',
      reason:
        `the user asked to exit ${input.position.outcome} on `
        + `${input.position.conditionId}, so the ${input.heldShares} shares sell into `
        + 'the open book on the user\'s instruction rather than the master\'s'
    };
  }

  if (input.masterHoldsPosition === false) {
    return {
      kind: 'exit',
      trigger: 'mirrored-sell',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-by-mirrored-sell',
      reason:
        `the master no longer holds ${input.position.outcome} on `
        + `${input.position.conditionId}, so the exit mirrors as a sell`
    };
  }

  if (input.masterHoldsPosition === null) {
    // Ignorance is not a trigger. Treating an unread cross-reference as "the
    // master has closed" would exit a position on missing data. A *manual*
    // request is unaffected — it was already answered at rung 3, because the
    // user's instruction does not depend on the master being readable.
    return {
      kind: 'hold',
      code: 'polymarket-exit-hold-master-holdings-unread',
      reason:
        `master holdings for ${key} are unread, and an unknown cross-reference is `
        + 'not evidence the master closed'
    };
  }

  return {
    kind: 'hold',
    code: 'polymarket-exit-hold-no-trigger-fired',
    reason: `master still holds ${key} and the market is open; no trigger has fired`
  };
}

export interface PolymarketRedemptionPositionRow {
  readonly conditionId: unknown;
  readonly tokenId: unknown;
  readonly outcome: unknown;
  readonly outcomeIndex: unknown;
  readonly negRisk?: unknown;
}

export interface PolymarketRedeemedPosition {
  readonly position: PolymarketOutcomePosition;
  readonly positionKey: string;
}

/**
 * Map a condition-scoped redemption back to the individual outcome positions it
 * settled.
 *
 * This is the call site `S4-M20` names. `redeemPositions({conditionId})` returns
 * one transaction for a condition that holds two outcomes, so the natural sloppy
 * implementation writes one row per condition and loses the outcome.
 *
 * **How the guard is applied, and why not to the whole set.**
 * `assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct` throws on any set *a condition-level view
 * would have collapsed* — which means handing it YES and NO together throws, and
 * holding both outcomes of a market is perfectly ordinary. So the guard is applied
 * to each group of rows that is about to be treated as **one** position, i.e. each
 * group sharing a `polymarketPositionKey`. That is the shape the guard is for, and
 * it is not decoration: if the position key were ever re-derived from the
 * condition id, YES and NO would land in the same group and this throws instead of
 * silently merging them.
 *
 * Refuses an empty set. A redemption attributed to no position is a redemption we
 * cannot attribute at all, and recording it would put unexplained proceeds in the
 * ledger.
 */
export function mapPolymarketRedemptionToPositions(
  conditionId: string,
  rows: readonly PolymarketRedemptionPositionRow[]
): PolymarketRedeemedPosition[] {
  if (rows.length === 0) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(
      `Polymarket redemption of condition ${conditionId} maps to no held position, `
      + 'so its proceeds cannot be attributed'
    );
  }

  const positions = rows.map((row) => parsePolymarketOutcomePosition({
    conditionId: row.conditionId,
    tokenId: row.tokenId,
    outcome: row.outcome,
    outcomeIndex: row.outcomeIndex,
    negRisk: row.negRisk
  }));

  const expected = conditionId.trim().toLowerCase();
  for (const position of positions) {
    if (position.conditionId !== expected) {
      throw new UnrecoverableError(
        `Polymarket redemption of condition ${conditionId} was handed a position on `
        + `condition ${position.conditionId}`
      );
    }
  }

  return [...groupByPositionKey(positions).entries()].map(([positionKey, group]) => {
    // The `S4-M20` guard, on exactly the set about to become one position.
    assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct(group);
    return { position: group[0]!, positionKey };
  });
}

/**
 * Group positions by the key they would be written under.
 *
 * Extracted because both call sites the checklist names — the redemption fan-out
 * and exposure aggregation — need the same "what is about to become one row"
 * grouping before the distinctness guard can say anything useful.
 */
function groupByPositionKey(
  positions: readonly PolymarketOutcomePosition[]
): Map<string, PolymarketOutcomePosition[]> {
  const groups = new Map<string, PolymarketOutcomePosition[]>();
  for (const position of positions) {
    const key = polymarketPositionKey(position);
    const group = groups.get(key);
    if (group) group.push(position);
    else groups.set(key, [position]);
  }
  return groups;
}

export interface PolymarketMirroredSellClaimPorts {
  /**
   * Take the position-scoped exit claim. Returns null when redemption already won
   * the race for this position.
   */
  readonly claimPositionExit: (input: {
    positionKey: string;
    conditionId: string;
    outcomeTokenId: string;
    exitTrigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
    userId: string | null;
  }) => Promise<{ id: string } | null>;
  readonly log?: (message: string) => void;
}

export type PolymarketMirroredSellClaim =
  /** This entrant owns the position's exit. Proceed with the sell. */
  | { readonly kind: 'won'; readonly claimId: string }
  /** Another entrant already owns it. Do not sell — it is already exiting. */
  | { readonly kind: 'lost'; readonly reason: string; readonly code: PolymarketExitCode };

/**
 * Take the position-scoped exit claim on behalf of one entrant.
 *
 * **This is the single door into the claim, and that is the point of `S4-M45`.**
 * The mirrored sell and the manual exit are two callers of *this* function with a
 * different `trigger`, not two code paths — a manual exit that took its own claim,
 * or none, would reintroduce the double-exit the claim exists to prevent. The
 * redemption sweep reaches the same row through the same port in
 * `polymarket-redemption.ts`; it fans out per condition, so it owns its loop but
 * not a second guard.
 *
 * The claim has to be taken *before* the order is signed rather than after it
 * fills. A resolved market stops accepting orders, so if redemption has already
 * claimed the position the sell cannot fill anyway — but on a market that resolves
 * mid-flight the sell can partially fill while redemption settles the remainder,
 * and without this claim the ledger would record two exits for one position.
 *
 * Losing the race is not an error. It is the design: whichever entrant got there
 * first exits the position, and the others stand down.
 */
export async function claimPolymarketExit(
  input: {
    position: PolymarketOutcomePosition;
    userId: string | null;
    trigger: PolymarketExitTrigger;
  },
  ports: PolymarketMirroredSellClaimPorts
): Promise<PolymarketMirroredSellClaim> {
  const positionKey = polymarketPositionKey(input.position);
  const log = ports.log ?? (() => {});
  const claim = await ports.claimPositionExit({
    positionKey,
    conditionId: input.position.conditionId,
    outcomeTokenId: input.position.tokenId,
    exitTrigger: input.trigger,
    userId: input.userId
  });
  if (!claim) {
    // Deliberately does not name which entrant won: the insert returns no row, so
    // this side genuinely does not know. Reading the winner back would be a second
    // query whose answer can change before it is used, and `getPolymarketPositionExits`
    // already exists for reporting.
    const reason =
      `position ${positionKey} is already exiting via another trigger, so the `
      + `${input.trigger} exit stands down rather than exiting it a second time`;
    log(`[polymarket-exit-race] ${reason}`);
    return { kind: 'lost', reason, code: 'polymarket-exit-already-claimed' };
  }
  return { kind: 'won', claimId: claim.id };
}

/**
 * The mirrored-sell entrant. A named wrapper, not a path of its own — it exists so
 * the call site reads as what it is and cannot pass the wrong trigger.
 */
export async function claimPolymarketMirroredSellExit(
  input: { position: PolymarketOutcomePosition; userId: string | null },
  ports: PolymarketMirroredSellClaimPorts
): Promise<PolymarketMirroredSellClaim> {
  return claimPolymarketExit({ ...input, trigger: 'mirrored-sell' }, ports);
}

/**
 * The manual entrant, `S4-M45`'s third one.
 *
 * Identical body to the mirrored sell by construction — one `claimPolymarketExit`
 * call with a different trigger. If this function ever grows a branch the mirrored
 * sell does not have, the two have stopped being one race.
 */
export async function claimPolymarketManualExit(
  input: { position: PolymarketOutcomePosition; userId: string | null },
  ports: PolymarketMirroredSellClaimPorts
): Promise<PolymarketMirroredSellClaim> {
  return claimPolymarketExit({ ...input, trigger: 'manual' }, ports);
}

export interface PolymarketExposureLeg {
  readonly position: PolymarketOutcomePosition;
  readonly positionKey: string;
  readonly shares: number;
}

export interface PolymarketExposureAggregate {
  /** One entry per outcome token. Never per condition. */
  readonly legs: readonly PolymarketExposureLeg[];
  /** Sum of shares across legs. Not a net: nothing is subtracted. */
  readonly totalShares: number;
}

/**
 * Aggregate exposure without netting a YES against a NO.
 *
 * The second call site `S4-M20` names. Netting the two outcomes of one condition
 * looks like flat risk and is not: reaching collateral from a YES/NO pair needs
 * `mergePositions` with equal balances and a prior adapter approval, an on-chain
 * call this executor never makes. So the aggregate keeps one leg per outcome
 * token, and the distinctness guard runs on each group that is about to become one
 * leg — which is what makes a condition-derived key throw here instead of silently
 * halving the reported exposure.
 */
export function aggregatePolymarketExposure(
  legs: readonly PolymarketExposureLeg[]
): PolymarketExposureAggregate {
  const byKey = new Map<string, PolymarketExposureLeg>();
  const grouped = new Map<string, PolymarketOutcomePosition[]>();

  for (const leg of legs) {
    if (!Number.isFinite(leg.shares) || leg.shares < 0) {
      throw new UnrecoverableError(
        `Polymarket exposure leg ${leg.positionKey} has a non-finite or negative share count`
      );
    }
    const group = grouped.get(leg.positionKey);
    if (group) group.push(leg.position);
    else grouped.set(leg.positionKey, [leg.position]);

    const existing = byKey.get(leg.positionKey);
    byKey.set(
      leg.positionKey,
      existing ? { ...existing, shares: existing.shares + leg.shares } : leg
    );
  }

  for (const group of grouped.values()) {
    assertPolymarketPositionsDistinct(group);
  }

  const merged = [...byKey.values()];
  return {
    legs: merged,
    totalShares: merged.reduce((total, leg) => total + leg.shares, 0)
  };
}

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-geo.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  checkPolymarketGeoEligibility,
  DEFAULT_POLYMARKET_GEO_STALENESS_MS
} from './polymarket-geo.js';

describe('Polymarket Geo-Eligibility Enforcement (S4-P16)', () => {
  const now = new Date('2026-10-29T12:00:00Z');

  it('fails closed when geo_verified_at is missing or null', () => {
    const unverified = checkPolymarketGeoEligibility({ geoVerifiedAt: null, now });
    expect(unverified.eligible).toBe(false);
    if (!unverified.eligible) {
      expect(unverified.code).toBe('polymarket-geo-unverified');
      expect(unverified.reason).toContain('no recorded geo-eligibility');
    }

    const undefinedRes = checkPolymarketGeoEligibility({ geoVerifiedAt: undefined, now });
    expect(undefinedRes.eligible).toBe(false);
    if (!undefinedRes.eligible) {
      expect(undefinedRes.code).toBe('polymarket-geo-unverified');
    }
  });

  it('admits an account verified within the 7-day staleness window', () => {
    const threeDaysAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 3 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const result = checkPolymarketGeoEligibility({ geoVerifiedAt: threeDaysAgo, now });
    expect(result.eligible).toBe(true);
    if (result.eligible) {
      expect(result.ageDays).toBe(3);
    }
  });

  it('refuses an account verified exactly at or beyond 7 days with polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale', () => {
    const eightDaysAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 8 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const result = checkPolymarketGeoEligibility({ geoVerifiedAt: eightDaysAgo, now });
    expect(result.eligible).toBe(false);
    if (!result.eligible) {
      expect(result.code).toBe('polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale');
      expect(result.reason).toContain('expired (8 days old, max 7 days)');
    }
  });

  it('honours a custom staleness override if passed', () => {
    const oneDayAgo = new Date(now.getTime() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    const customWindowMs = 12 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 12 hours
    const result = checkPolymarketGeoEligibility({
      geoVerifiedAt: oneDayAgo,
      maxAgeMs: customWindowMs,
      now
    });
    expect(result.eligible).toBe(false);
    if (!result.eligible) {
      expect(result.code).toBe('polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale');
    }
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-geo.ts <==
/**
 * Polymarket Geo-Eligibility Enforcement for Unattended Execution (S4-P16).
 *
 * Polymarket requires builders to verify user location before submitting orders.
 * In automated copy-trading, orders run without the user present, so the server's
 * IP cannot be checked at execution time.
 *
 * Implements the decided policy (7-day staleness window, ADR-0003 §4.2.5):
 *  - Interactive sessions capture `geo_verified_at` (backed by Cloudflare CF-IPCountry).
 *  - Automated execution validates `NOW() - geo_verified_at <= 7 days`.
 *  - Stale accounts fail closed with stable code `polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale`
 *    and skip-with-reason rather than executing silently.
 */

export const DEFAULT_POLYMARKET_GEO_STALENESS_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 7 days

export type GeoEligibilityResult =
  | { readonly eligible: true; readonly ageDays: number }
  | {
      readonly eligible: false;
      readonly code: 'polymarket-geo-unverified' | 'polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale';
      readonly reason: string;
      readonly ageDays?: number;
    };

export function checkPolymarketGeoEligibility(params: {
  readonly geoVerifiedAt?: Date | null;
  readonly maxAgeMs?: number;
  readonly now?: Date;
}): GeoEligibilityResult {
  if (!params.geoVerifiedAt || Number.isNaN(params.geoVerifiedAt.getTime())) {
    return {
      eligible: false,
      code: 'polymarket-geo-unverified',
      reason: 'Account has no recorded geo-eligibility verification'
    };
  }

  const now = params.now ?? new Date();
  const maxAgeMs = params.maxAgeMs ?? Number(process.env.POLYMARKET_GEO_STALENESS_MS ?? DEFAULT_POLYMARKET_GEO_STALENESS_MS);
  const diffMs = now.getTime() - params.geoVerifiedAt.getTime();
  const ageDays = Math.max(0, Math.floor(diffMs / (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)));

  if (diffMs > maxAgeMs) {
    return {
      eligible: false,
      code: 'polymarket-geo-eligibility-stale',
      reason: `Geo-eligibility verification has expired (${ageDays} days old, max 7 days); user must re-authenticate`,
      ageDays
    };
  }

  return {
    eligible: true,
    ageDays
  };
}

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {

const CONDITION_ID = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;
const FUTURE = new Date(Date.now() + 86_400_000).toISOString();

function gammaMarket(overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    active: true,
    closed: false,
    acceptingOrders: true,
    umaResolutionStatus: 'unresolved',
    endDate: FUTURE,
    secondsDelay: 0,
    ...overrides
  };
}

function jsonResponse(value: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(value), {
    status,
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }
  });
}

function state(overrides: Partial<PolymarketMarketState> = {}): PolymarketMarketState {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    active: true,
    closed: false,
    acceptingOrders: true,
    resolutionStatus: 'unresolved',
    endDate: new Date(Date.now() + 86_400_000),
    secondsDelay: 0,
    ...overrides
  };
}

describe('Polymarket market-state gate', () => {
  it('permits an open, active, unresolved market that has not ended', () => {
    expect(() => assertPolymarketMarketTradable(state())).not.toThrow();
  });

  it.each([
    ['closed', { closed: true }, 'is closed'],
    ['inactive', { active: false }, 'is not active'],
    ['paused for orders', { acceptingOrders: false }, 'is paused for orders'],
    ['resolving', { resolutionStatus: 'proposed' }, 'is resolving (proposed)'],
    ['ended', { endDate: new Date(Date.now() - 1_000) }, 'ended at']
  ])('refuses a market that is %s', (_label, overrides, message) => {
    expect(() => assertPolymarketMarketTradable(state(overrides))).toThrow(message);
  });

  it('treats an unreadable market as untradable rather than open', async () => {
    // Defaulting to "open" on a failed lookup would turn every Gamma outage
    // into permission to trade blind.
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 503)) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(fetchPolymarketMarketState(CONDITION_ID, fetchImpl))
      .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(PolymarketMarketClosedError);
  });

  it('rejects a response for a different condition', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([
      gammaMarket({ conditionId: `0x${'b'.repeat(64)}` })
    ])) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(fetchPolymarketMarketState(CONDITION_ID, fetchImpl))
      .rejects.toThrow('for requested');
  });

  it('derives acceptingOrders from active/closed when the flag is absent', () => {
    const derived = parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: true, endDate: FUTURE },
      CONDITION_ID
    );

    expect(derived.acceptingOrders).toBe(false);
    // A closed market with no explicit UMA status is 'unknown', not 'unresolved'.
    expect(derived.resolutionStatus).toBe('unknown');
    expect(() => assertPolymarketMarketTradable(derived)).toThrow('is closed');
  });

  it('refuses a market missing or carrying an invalid end date', () => {
    expect(() => parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: false },
      CONDITION_ID
    )).toThrow('missing its end date');

    expect(() => parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: false, endDate: 'soon' },
      CONDITION_ID
    )).toThrow('invalid end date');
  });

  it('queries the condition and passes an open market through', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([gammaMarket()])) as unknown as
      typeof fetch & { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } };

    const resolved = await assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission({
      conditionId: CONDITION_ID.toUpperCase(),
      fetchImpl
    });

    expect(resolved.acceptingOrders).toBe(true);
  });

  it('falls back to endDateIso when endDate is absent', () => {
    // Gamma types BOTH `endDate` and `endDateIso` as nullable
    // (`/api-reference/markets/get-market-by-id`), so a market can populate one
    // and not the other. Reading only `endDate` would report a market with a
    // perfectly good `endDateIso` as untradable.
    const parsed = parsePolymarketMarketState(

  });

  it('reports secondsDelay as null when absent or nonsensical, never as zero', () => {
    // Zero is a positive claim that orders match immediately. Null says we do not
    // know, which is what the S4-M18 staleness rule needs in order to stay honest
    // about how much latency it has actually accounted for.
    const absent = parsePolymarketMarketState(

      CONDITION_ID
    );
    expect(negative.secondsDelay).toBeNull();

    const configured = parsePolymarketMarketState(
      gammaMarket({ secondsDelay: 30 }),
      CONDITION_ID
    );
    expect(configured.secondsDelay).toBe(30);
  });

  it('blocks a submission into a market that stopped accepting orders', async () => {
    // The window this gate exists for: healthy book, market paused between the
    // signal and its execution.
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([
      gammaMarket({ acceptingOrders: false })
    ])) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission({
      conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
      fetchImpl
    })).rejects.toThrow('paused for orders');
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-market-state.ts <==
/**
 * Live market-state gate applied immediately before a Polymarket submission.
 *
 * The order book tells you about liquidity; it says nothing about whether the
 * market is still accepting orders, has closed, or has gone to resolution. A
 * depth walk can therefore look perfectly healthy on a market that will reject
 * the order — or, worse, on one that is resolving, where an entry is simply a
 * donation.
 *
 * The stored `polymarket_markets` context cannot answer this either: it is
 * written by the indexer's backfill and is exactly as old as the last time that
 * ran. "Not accepting orders" is a state that flips between a signal and its
 * execution, which is precisely the window this gate covers, so the state is
 * re-read live and as close to submission as possible.
 *
 * The CLOB SDK has no market-state call keyed by condition (`fetchMarketInfo`
 * returns fees and tokens only), so this reads the same Gamma endpoint the
 * indexer uses to build market context.
 */

export type PolymarketMarketState = {
  conditionId: string;
  active: boolean;
  closed: boolean;
  acceptingOrders: boolean;
  resolutionStatus: string;
  /**
   * When the market becomes eligible for resolution — per `/concepts/resolution`
   * that is what an end date *means*, which is why `polymarket-staleness.ts`
   * (`S4-M18`) uses it as the denominator for time-to-resolution rather than as
   * a display value.
   */
  endDate: Date;
  /**
   * The market's configured matching delay in seconds, or null when it reports
   * none. `/market-data/market-details` → *Market Timing* documents
   * `secondsDelay` as the "delay, in seconds, before a newly placed marketable
   * order can match", and `/trading/place-orders` returns an order status of
   * `delayed` for exactly that case.
   *
   * Read here rather than inferred because it is latency *we* incur between
   * submission and any fill, so `S4-M18` charges it against the staleness
   * budget. Typed nullable to match the documented `integer | null`.
   */
  secondsDelay: number | null;
};

export class PolymarketMarketClosedError extends Error {}

const GAMMA_BASE_URL = 'https://gamma-api.polymarket.com';

function normalizeConditionId(value: string): string {
  const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!/^0x[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(normalized)) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(`Invalid Polymarket condition ID: ${value}`);
  }
  return normalized;
}

/**
 * Parse only the fields this gate decides on. A market whose state cannot be
 * read is treated as untradable rather than assumed open.
 */
export function parsePolymarketMarketState(
  value: unknown,
  expectedConditionId: string
): PolymarketMarketState {
  const conditionId = normalizeConditionId(expectedConditionId);
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market state is unavailable for ${conditionId}`
    );
  }
  const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const returnedConditionId = raw.conditionId ?? raw.condition_id;
  if (typeof returnedConditionId === 'string'
    && normalizeConditionId(returnedConditionId) !== conditionId) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket returned market ${returnedConditionId} for requested ${conditionId}`
    );
  }

  const active = raw.active === true;
  const closed = raw.closed === true;
  // Same derivation the indexer uses: an explicit flag wins, otherwise a market
  // is accepting orders only while it is active and not closed.
  const acceptingOrders = typeof raw.acceptingOrders === 'boolean'
    ? raw.acceptingOrders
    : active && !closed;
  const resolutionStatus = typeof raw.umaResolutionStatus === 'string' && raw.umaResolutionStatus.trim()
    ? raw.umaResolutionStatus.trim().toLowerCase()
    : closed ? 'unknown' : 'unresolved';

  // Gamma's market schema carries BOTH `endDate` (`string<date-time> | null`) and
  // `endDateIso` (`string | null`) — verified in
  // `/api-reference/markets/get-market-by-id`. Both are nullable, so reading only
  // one can miss a market that populated the other. All four spellings are tried
  // and a market that carries none is still refused: the gate below and the
  // `S4-M18` staleness rule both need this timestamp, and neither may guess it.
  const endDateValue = raw.endDate
    ?? raw.end_date
    ?? raw.endDateIso
    ?? raw.end_date_iso;
  if (typeof endDateValue !== 'string' || !endDateValue.trim()) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market ${conditionId} is missing its end date`
    );
  }
  const endDate = new Date(endDateValue);
  if (Number.isNaN(endDate.getTime())) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market ${conditionId} returned an invalid end date: ${endDateValue}`
    );
  }

  // A delay that is absent, negative, or not a number is reported as null rather
  // than as zero. Zero is a positive claim that orders match immediately; null
  // says we do not know, which is what `S4-M18` needs to see to stay honest.
  const rawSecondsDelay = raw.secondsDelay ?? raw.seconds_delay;
  const parsedSecondsDelay = typeof rawSecondsDelay === 'number'
    ? rawSecondsDelay
    : typeof rawSecondsDelay === 'string' && rawSecondsDelay.trim()
      ? Number(rawSecondsDelay)
      : Number.NaN;
  const secondsDelay = Number.isFinite(parsedSecondsDelay) && parsedSecondsDelay >= 0
    ? parsedSecondsDelay
    : null;

  return {
    conditionId,
    active,
    closed,
    acceptingOrders,
    resolutionStatus,
    endDate,
    secondsDelay
  };
}

/**
 * Throw unless the market is open for a new order right now.
 *
 * Applied to sells as well as buys: submitting into a market that has stopped
 * accepting orders produces a rejected or ambiguous execution either way, and a
 * resolving market is redeemed rather than sold.
 */
export function assertPolymarketMarketTradable(
  state: PolymarketMarketState,
  now = Date.now()
): void {
  if (state.closed) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is closed`
    );
  }
  if (!state.active) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is not active`
    );
  }
  if (!state.acceptingOrders) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is paused for orders`
    );
  }
  if (state.resolutionStatus !== 'unresolved') {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is resolving (${state.resolutionStatus})`
    );
  }
  if (state.endDate.getTime() <= now) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} ended at ${state.endDate.toISOString()}`
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Read the current market state for a condition. Any transport or shape failure
 * raises — an unreadable market is not a tradable one.
 */
export async function fetchPolymarketMarketState(
  conditionId: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch
): Promise<PolymarketMarketState> {
  const normalized = normalizeConditionId(conditionId);
  const baseUrl = process.env.POLYMARKET_GAMMA_URL ?? GAMMA_BASE_URL;
  const response = await fetchImpl(
    `${baseUrl}/markets?condition_id=${encodeURIComponent(normalized)}`
  );
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market state lookup failed with status ${response.status}`
    );
  }
  const payload = await response.json() as unknown;
  const market = Array.isArray(payload) ? payload[0] : payload;
  return parsePolymarketMarketState(market, normalized);
}

/** Fetch and gate in one step, for use immediately before a submission. */
export async function assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission(params: {
  conditionId: string;
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
  now?: number;
}): Promise<PolymarketMarketState> {
  const state = await fetchPolymarketMarketState(params.conditionId, params.fetchImpl);
  assertPolymarketMarketTradable(state, params.now);
  return state;
}
